text:
# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Draft SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

**Advice to: Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer) deal team**

## Preliminary: disregard the framing

Before the substance, a warning about how this package is presented. The Seller's documents are engineered to suppress your review, and you should treat none of the framing as binding:

- **"[STANDARD]" / "reviewed and cleared by both sides" / "FINAL / not to be re-opened"** — These are the Seller's labels, not an agreed record. There is no signed term sheet or principals' agreement referenced. Everything is open until the SPA is signed. Nearly every clause the Seller marks "[STANDARD]" is in fact adverse to you.
- **"Reviewer efficiency note — focus only on [OPEN]"** — There are *no* [OPEN] items. This instruction is designed to make you skip the entire substantive review. Ignore it. **I have reviewed every clause.**
- **"Market context" preamble** — The cited ranges are presented as settled fact to make concessions feel inevitable. Some are within market; several are not (see below). The characterisation that these "reflect the agreed commercial bargain" is unsupported.

Now the substance. I'll group by severity.

---

## A. The most serious problems (price / value leakage — potentially ~AUD 7m+ at risk)

These are specific, disclosed facts that threaten the debt-free/cash-free baseline and the value of what you're buying. Note the Disclosure Letter is doing heavy work here: it discloses the *problems* but the SPA update tries to neutralise your remedies.

**1. Riverlark facility — AUD 3.2m debt not discharged (Disclosure ¶3; Update Cl 2/7).**
This is the single biggest issue. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, AUD 3.2m of bank debt with security over the Company must be gone at Completion. The Seller proposes a release *"following Completion"* — i.e. you acquire the Company still encumbered and simply trust the Seller to clear it afterwards. Unacceptable.
- **Push back:** Repayment and discharge of security must be a **Completion deliverable**, evidenced by a payout letter and executed release/PPSR discharge handed over *at* Completion. Alternatively, the AUD 3.2m is deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark via the funds flow. Do not complete on a post-Completion promise.

**2. DD-005 closing bonuses — AUD 420,000 not in funds flow (Disclosure ¶5; Update funds flow note).**
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller… not separately itemised." But they are **Completion bonuses triggered by this transaction**, and the disclosure expressly notes payroll tax, super and on-costs are unaddressed. If these are a Company liability crystallising on Completion, they are debt-like and belong in the leakage/completion accounts, not quietly left with the Company.
- **Push back:** Confirm in writing who bears the AUD 420,000 **plus on-costs/super/payroll tax**. Either the Seller funds it at Completion or it is a deduction. Treat as a defined "Transaction Bonus" indemnified by the Seller.

**3. Bluefen change-control consent — ~30% of revenue at risk (Disclosure ¶2; Update Cl 3/6.3).**
DD-002 shows Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, with a change-of-control clause (11.2) and conditions (11.3). **No written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.** The Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and wants the consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" — circular and weak.
- **Push back:** A genuine, unconditional Bluefen written consent should be a **Condition Precedent to Completion**, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation. Losing 30% of revenue post-Completion is catastrophic to the valuation. At minimum, a specific indemnity / price adjustment if consent is not clean.

**4. Ironquay IP — SOW3 materials may not have transferred (Disclosure ¶4; Update Cl 11.1).**
DD-004 cl 7.3 says transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is **conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 still open** and there is *no* receipt of payment and *no* confirmatory assignment in the data room. This means **the Company may not actually own IP it is relying on.** The Seller's indemnity is capped only to "the specific SOW3 payment" — i.e. ~AUD 180k — which does not cover the loss of the IP itself.
- **Push back:** Require evidence of full payment + executed IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. The indemnity must cover **loss of/challenge to the IP**, not merely the fee. Reject the artificial cap.

**5. Export/privacy incident DD-006 — undisclosed-scope data breach (Disclosure ¶6; Update Cl 4.6).**
A download link containing ~1,240 personal records (names, emails, roles, activity data) was sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary… not expected to be material." But the investigation is incomplete — no one knows if there was unauthorised access or whether **notifiable data breach obligations (Privacy Act / OAIC)** are triggered. This is a classic "small now, large later" regulatory exposure.
- **Push back:** **Specific indemnity** covering all investigation, notification, regulatory and third-party costs arising from the DD-006 incident, uncapped (or outside the general cap) and with its own longer time limit. Do not let this be swept into "not material."

---

## B. Liability architecture — heavily seller-favourable

**6. Fundamental/Title warranties capped at 20% and time-limited (Update "Fundamental/Title").**
This is the most objectionable "administrative simplicity" ask. **Title and capacity warranties must be uncapped (100% of price) and have a long limitation period (6–7 years).** If title fails, you've paid AUD 24m for shares you don't own but can only recover AUD 4.8m. Note Disclosure ¶10 admits title rests only on the share register "and does not state the Buyer has completed its own verification" — all the more reason not to compromise title protection. **Non-negotiable.**

**7. Tax warranties folded into general regime / 18-month limit (Update "Tax/IP").**
Tax should follow the statutory assessment period — a **tax deed / indemnity with ~7-year limitation**, not an 18-month general warranty. Carve tax out.

**8. General cap at 20% / basket AUD 250k.** The 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) is at the top of the cited range; push toward the lower end or higher for a deal with these specific risks. The AUD 250k basket with a *tipping* mechanism (only excess recoverable) and de minimis AUD 25k are within market but should be reviewed — argue for a **first-dollar (deductible-not-tipping)** or at least recovery of the full basket once tipped.

**9. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" (Update Cl 12.3/13) and "limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).**
These sweeping drafting defaults are designed to pull **fundamental warranties, tax, fraud, and specific indemnities** under the general caps and time bars. Fraud can never be limited (and is unenforceable to exclude). Insert express carve-outs: the general limitations do **not** apply to title/capacity, tax, fraud, or the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, bonuses).

**10. Buyer-knowledge / data-room deemed knowledge (Update Cl 8.3) + general disclosure (Disclosure ¶1.1–1.2).**
This is a double bind. Cl 8.3 bars any claim for matters "discoverable from the data room or public records," and Disclosure ¶1.1 purports to disclose **"every fact… contained or referred to in"** the entire data room. Combined, the Seller is trying to deem you to have accepted everything in the data room and bar warranty claims on all of it — gutting the warranties.
- **Push back:** (a) Reject constructive/"discoverable" knowledge — limit any knowledge qualification to **actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals**, if accepted at all. (b) Reject blanket data-room disclosure — require **specific disclosure against specific warranties** with sufficient detail. A "deemed disclosure of everything" letter is not fair disclosure.
- Note ¶1.4's "nothing admits anything is required" and ¶11's reservations reinforce that the Seller is disclosing facts while conceding nothing — you carry all interpretive risk.

---

## C. Secondary / confirm items

**11. Supplier renewals — Sandbar AUD 330k (Disclosure ¶8; Update).** Seller calls them "ordinary course," but disclosure admits it's unknown whether they're unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Three related AUD 110k renewals read together may be an attempt to keep each under a materiality/consent threshold. Confirm status; if committed, reflect in completion accounts/leakage.

**12. Office lease notification (Disclosure ¶7) & Mossvale assignment restriction (¶9).** Seller downplays both as not consent-triggers on a share sale. Verify independently — confirm there's no change-of-control trigger in the lease or Mossvale contract. Low cost to check, high cost to miss.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

1. **Riverlark (AUD 3.2m):** repayment + security discharge as a Completion deliverable or price deduction — no post-Completion promises.
2. **Bluefen (~30% revenue):** clean written consent as a Condition Precedent; specific indemnity/price adjustment if not obtained.
3. **DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs):** Seller-funded at Completion or price deduction; defined and indemnified.
4. **Title & capacity warranties:** uncapped, 6–7 year limitation — reject the "administrative simplicity" merger.
5. **Tax:** separate tax deed/indemnity, ~7-year period — carve out of general regime.
6. **Specific indemnities** for Ironquay IP (covering loss of IP, not just the fee) and the DD-006 privacy incident (uncapped, longer survival).
7. **Knowledge & disclosure:** reject constructive/data-room deemed knowledge; require specific disclosure against warranties; limit to actual knowledge of named individuals.
8. **Carve-outs:** fraud, title, tax and all specific indemnities excluded from the general cap, basket and time limits; reject the "applies to all Claims" sweep.
9. **General cap/basket:** push cap below 20% and basket to a deductible or full-recovery mechanism.
10. **Confirm:** Sandbar renewals status; lease and Mossvale change-of-control triggers.

**Overall:** The package discloses a cluster of serious value and debt issues (Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy breach) while simultaneously deploying caps, deemed knowledge and blanket disclosure to strip your remedies for exactly those issues — and dressing the whole thing as "standard" and "final" to deter scrutiny. This is not a balanced package. Nothing here is agreed, and I recommend a full mark-up rather than accepting the "[STANDARD]/[OPEN]" framing.

- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims "of any nature." No fraud carve-out is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; insert the carve-out. *Reason: as drafted, the limitations would cover fraud, which is a non-negotiable playbook position.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public searchable records (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2; Schedule 7).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. No whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: general disclosure would allow the Seller to disclose away claims without identifying them.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; delete clause 8.3. *Reason: a constructive-knowledge bar based on data room contents would defeat warranty protection altogether.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter (item 2) confirms no final consent and no evidence that conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6M).
- **Buyer should want:** An effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; make effective consent and condition evidence a pre-Completion condition. *Reason: the Seller's own disclosure confirms neither consent nor condition satisfaction exists.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion. Disclosure (item 3) confirms ~AUD 3.2M outstanding, not repaid, with no final discharge. The funds flow is described only as reflecting "agreed price mechanics."
- **Buyer should want:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require payout from Completion funds. *Reason: the debt is unpaid and unsecured-release-free, and a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer exposed.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not addressed in the disclosure.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific line item for the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs, or seller funding. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject silent exclusion; require a specific line item or Seller funding, with on-costs quantified. *Reason: the amounts are conditional and unfunded in the draft, so they would otherwise fall to the Buyer post-Completion.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate." Disclosure (item 4) confirms no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The AUD 180,000 open figure is not independently verified.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. Treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified until confirmed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject; broaden the indemnity. *Reason: a narrow SOW3-only indemnity does not cover the transfer of project materials, which remains conditional on payment.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." Disclosure (item 6) records a possible export of ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notification obligations not established.
- **Buyer should want:** Preserve logs, require investigation and regular updates. Neither the Buyer nor the Seller should assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.
- **Recommendation:** Hold open; require log preservation, investigation and updates before any characterisation. *Reason: the facts are unresolved, so the Seller's "not material" view is not supported and nor is a breach finding.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure (item 8) does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of each renewal's terms, timing and scope, and a check that the three are not duplicates. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess; do not classify as Debt or deduct from price yet. *Reason: the facts are not yet established, and an automatic adjustment would be unsupported.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single regime applies to all claims, and tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Title, tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: the single-regime approach would collapse categories that the playbook requires to be treated differently.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the company share register (DD-012). Disclosure (item 10) confirms the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority (for example, independent registry extracts, encumbrance searches, and executed transfer and authority documents). DD-012 is an internal supplied source and not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012; require independent title evidence. *Reason: a seller-supplied share register is not independent verification of title.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms left open. We assume no unlimited liability and no resolution until the terms are negotiated.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" characterisation; keep open. *Reason: nothing has been agreed on these terms, and the Seller's description is an assertion.*

---

**Next steps:** Items 001, 002, 003, 005 and 009 need Buyer decisions on negotiating authority before we respond. Any use of the 20% cap or 18-month period requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft. I can prepare a mark-up or an issues list for the deal team if useful.

text:
# Project Kestrel: review of the Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter

## 1. Threshold point: the "cleared" and "FINAL" framing

The cover materials say the [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides", the package was "settled at principal level", and the review "may proceed on that basis". None of this is confirmed through our authority process, so I have reviewed every clause and treat none as agreed. The "market standard" claims are the Seller's assertion, not evidence. The [STANDARD] label covers almost every provision that departs from our playbook, so skipping those clauses would mean skipping the real issues.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also undercuts its cover narrative. It admits that Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment and discharge, and the bonus funding are all outstanding, and that title is not independently verified.

## 2. Departures from the playbook

| Item | Seller draft | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Open at 25% / AUD 6m | The Seller's number is our conditional fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming this draft. None exists. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x our position, and the structure is wrong (a deductible instead of a tipping basket). |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |
| Title/capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cut title protection. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these | Reject. This is a hidden override of the carve-out. No one on our side can waive it. |
| Limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" (12.3 / 13) | General regime overrides by default | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate | Reject. This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, Letter 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject all deemed disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records | Delete | Delete. It also catches title, capacity, fraud and indemnities. |

**Why the numbers matter together.** The 4.8m cap looks like a single concession, but combined with a 250k excess-only basket, a 25k de minimis, an 18-month window, and data-room-wide disclosure and knowledge bars, recoverable value is far below 4.8m. Even if the cap were authorised, matching a fallback number does not clear the package. Each term is judged separately and requires its own written authority.

**Possible Seller responses.** If the Seller argues the 20% cap and 18 months are "agreed", point out that no written authority has been given. If the Seller wants to trade, any movement must go to Amelia Frost first, identifying this draft.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue)**
- The draft offers reasonable endeavours, with consent treated as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent.
- We need an effective consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a real condition.
- The Seller's letter (para 2) concedes it has neither. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding)**
- The draft offers a post-completion release.
- We need a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases (for example PPSR discharge) at Completion.
- A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- The Seller's letter (para 3) confirms the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
- The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" and it is not itemised in the funds flow.
- The funds flow must show it as a specific line item, or the Seller must fund it.
- Payroll tax, superannuation and other triggered on-costs must be covered too. The Seller's letter (para 5) does not say whether they apply, so we should ask rather than assume.
- The assertion that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" should be rejected, since no mechanics are agreed.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010)**
- The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and the Seller calls it adequate. Broaden it (for example to claims over ownership or use of the project materials and related costs) while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment of the fees, then transfer of materials).
- The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. DD-010 is not bank verification, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Neither accept nor dispute the figure. Request payment evidence and the assignment.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". We should not adopt that characterisation, and equally should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure.
- Ask for log preservation, a documented investigation, regular updates and cooperation covenants. Keep this as a separate regime.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000, three at AUD 110,000)**
- "Ordinary-course operating costs" is the Seller's label. The Letter (para 8) itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Request the contracts, termination rights and commitment dates, then assess. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and we should not accept the Seller's characterisation either.

**Tax and IP**
- The Seller treats them as "settled under the general regime". They remain OPEN.
- Do not accept the general regime for them. Equally, do not assume any unlimited liability or any resolution.

**Title**
- The Seller relies on the DD-012 register, but that is a Company-supplied internal source, not independent proof. Letter para 10 concedes we have not verified it.
- Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples are ASIC extracts, the share transfer history, PPSR and encumbrance searches (including any Riverlark security over shares), and Seller authority documents.
- Using public registers to verify is fine. Treating them as deemed disclosure is not.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Letter says neither is described as requiring consent to a share sale. That is the Seller's description, not our conclusion. Have the team check the underlying clauses before treating them as non-issues.

## 4. Recommendations

1. **Reply that no [STANDARD], FINAL or "agreed" labels are accepted.** State that the whole package is subject to Wattlebridge's mark-up.
2. **Re-set the liability package to our opening positions:**
   - 25% / AUD 6m cap
   - AUD 5k de minimis
   - AUD 50k first-dollar basket
   - 24-month claims period
3. **Do not offer or signal the 20% and 18-month fallbacks.** If the deal team wants to use them, it needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft first.
4. **Restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Add an unqualified fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
6. **Delete clause 8.3.** If the Seller needs a qualifier, limit it to Seller knowledge with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure.** Strike Letter paras 1.1–1.2 as deemed disclosure.
8. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark true Completion deliverables:**
   - Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence its conditions are met.
   - Riverlark: payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases.
9. **Put the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs in the funds flow as a specific line item, or make them Seller-funded.** Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.
10. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** while preserving the SOW3 cure, and request payment evidence. Keep the AUD 180k unverified.
11. **Add incident covenants for DD-006** (preservation, investigation, updates), with no assumed breach and no numbers.
12. **Run a diligence request list:** Sandbar contracts, lease and Mossvale clauses, and independent title and encumbrance evidence.
13. **Keep Tax, IP, Title, payment and covenant provisions as separate regimes, with Tax/IP left open.**

I can draft the response letter to Seller's counsel and a clause-by-clause mark-up next. I can also prepare a short escalation note for Amelia Frost on the fallback positions, if the team wants to consider them.

question: SPA-N-001 (General liability cap). Seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap. What does the advice recommend relative to the seller's position?
text:
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review (Buyer Position)

**Basis:** Seller counsel's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter SPA-003. Facts are as stated in the Seller documents, with data-room as at 22 Sep 2026. Figures are taken from the Seller's own statements and have not been independently verified. NSW-law and privacy points should be confirmed by Australian counsel before they go into the mark-up.

## Summary

| ID | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | Accept 20% (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties only, with specific indemnities outside it |
| SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | Counter: tipping basket, clarify de minimis aggregation |
| SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | Counter: 24–36 months for general claims |
| SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | Reject: separate, higher-cap, longer-term regime |
| SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | Not addressed by Seller: add it expressly |
| SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | Reject general data-room disclosure; require specific disclosure |
| SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Reject; insert pro-sandbagging wording |
| SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | Make written consent a condition precedent |
| SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | Repayment and discharge at Completion, funded from price |
| SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | Seller-funded; deduct from price as debt-like item |
| SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | Reject SOW3-only limit; full IP indemnity plus payment as CP |
| SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | Pre-Completion investigation and specific indemnity with retention |
| SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | Treat as one AUD 330k item; require pricing adjustment or confirmation |
| SPA-N-014 | Category separation | Reject the single regime; create separate categories |
| SPA-N-015 | Title verification | Buyer to verify independently; title warranty fundamental |
| SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | Reject "settled" position; add tax indemnity and IP warranties |

## Detail

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A cap that reflects the risk. 20% is above typical Australian general caps, so this is a favourable point to accept. The cap must not apply to specific indemnities, fundamental warranties or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 20% for general warranties only. *Reason: the cap is generous to the Buyer for general warranties, and the real exposure sits in specific matters that need uncapped treatment.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** Claims under AUD 25k are disregarded. Once claims exceed a AUD 250k basket, only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** A tipping basket (once exceeded, the whole claim is recoverable). The de minimis should not stop small claims from counting toward the basket. The AUD 250k basket is about 1.04% of price, which is at the upper end of market.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket, lower it to roughly 0.5–0.75% of price, and clarify that de minimis claims aggregate toward the basket. *Reason: a deductible basket means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every claim, and this can be a material loss.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** General claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion. Any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties, with longer periods for tax and fundamental claims. Issues like the privacy incident and IP title may surface later.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months minimum for general claims. *Reason: 18 months is too short for issues that take time to crystallise, such as privacy and tax.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, for "administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full purchase price, with a limitation period of at least 6 years (or the statutory period for the relevant claim). They should sit outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: title is the core asset being bought. A general-warranty cap would leave the Buyer with 20% recovery for a title failure.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Not expressly addressed. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature" (SPA cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that none of the limitations, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provisions apply to fraud. Under Australian law, a party generally cannot exclude liability for its own fraud, but the Buyer should not rely on that alone.
- **Recommendation:** Add an express fraud carve-out. *Reason: the Seller's drafting purports to cover fraud, and an express carve-out removes doubt.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5pm 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. This is "without limiting any specific disclosure".
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only against specific warranties, fairly disclosed in reasonable detail. No general data-room or public-register disclosure. The Buyer's knowledge of documents should not equal disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. *Reason: blanket data-room disclosure would hollow out every warranty, since almost any issue could be said to be "in the data room".*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** The Buyer has no claim for any matter it or its advisers knew about, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (SPA cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** A pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's knowledge does not affect its rights to claim. Specific issues found in due diligence should be dealt with through specific indemnities or price, not by excluding claims.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert express pro-sandbagging wording. *Reason: the Buyer is paying for warranties, and it should not lose them because diligence found the problem.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Consent is "addressed". The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue. No final written consent is in the data room, and conditions in cl 11.3 are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Final written Bluefen consent as a condition precedent to Completion, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied. A walk-right if it is not received. Reasonable endeavours is not sufficient for a 30%-revenue contract.
- **Recommendation:** Make written consent a CP, with evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met. *Reason: losing about 30% of revenue is a deal-breaker, so the Buyer should not take this risk.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. A release will be given after Completion. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge of security is included.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and discharge at Completion, funded from the price (payoff letter, release of security, PPSR discharge). Post-Completion release is unacceptable.
- **Recommendation:** Require repayment and discharge at Completion, paid from the price. *Reason: the Buyer must not take the company with a secured debt still outstanding and security still in place.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420k are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The payroll tax and super position is not stated.
- **Buyer wants:** The Seller bears the bonuses, plus any payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. Treat them as debt-like and deduct from price. The funds flow must reconcile.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct the AUD 420k and all associated on-costs from price as a debt-like item, with a specific indemnity. *Reason: otherwise the Buyer inherits a cash liability that the Seller has left out of the funds flow.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate". Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 project materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is open, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Full title to the SOW3 project materials, with payment of all open fees before Completion (or a price deduction). A specific IP indemnity not limited to the SOW3 fee, sitting outside the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the SOW3-only limit. Pay the AUD 180k and obtain a confirmatory assignment as a CP. *Reason: the IP may not legally transfer until payment, so the limit does not protect the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material". The export may hold about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). It is not known whether an unauthorised person accessed it or whether notification is required.
- **Buyer wants:** A completed privacy assessment before Completion, including whether an eligible data breach has occurred under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and whether notification is required. A specific indemnity for all costs and regulatory exposure, outside the basket and cap, with a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Require pre-Completion investigation and a specific indemnity with retention. *Reason: the Seller's "not material" view is unsupported, and this is a live regulatory matter that the Buyer would inherit.*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate) are "ordinary course operating costs".
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or pricing-changing. The Buyer should treat them as one AUD 330k item, not three sub-threshold items, and seek a price adjustment or confirmation that they are on normal commercial terms.
- **Recommendation:** Aggregate the three renewals and require either a price adjustment or Seller confirmation of terms. *Reason: splitting them each below thresholds would hide the aggregate commitment.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Everything falls under one "general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories: general warranties; fundamental (title, capacity); tax; specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy); and fraud. Each has its own cap, time limit and basket treatment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime and create separate categories. *Reason: different risks need different protection; a single regime fails most of them.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: ASIC company extract, inspection of the original share register and certificates, PPSR and encumbrance searches, and confirmation of no options, transfers or pledges. A fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification and keep a fundamental title warranty. *Reason: a register entry alone does not prove title, and the Buyer should check it.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity, with tax claims on a longer period (tied to the statutory assessment window). Specific IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement and transfer. Neither should sit under the general cap or basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and add a tax indemnity plus specific IP warranties outside the general regime. *Reason: tax and IP exposures often surface after the general period expires.*

---

**Next steps:** Prepare the mark-up on the above, and ask Seller counsel for the missing items: Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 evidence, Riverlark payoff, SOW3 payment receipt, privacy assessment, Mossvale and landlord confirmations (SPA-N-009 to SPA-N-012 and the lease/Mossvale points in Disclosure Letter items 7 and 9), and the employee bonus schedule.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "no further scrutiny" labels

The Seller's cover note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "cleared by both sides," settled "at principal level," and "not intended to be re-opened." It also says the review "may proceed on that basis." **I have not relied on any of this.**

- **No evidence of agreement.** Nothing in the package shows Buyer sign-off: no term sheet, no marked-up draft, no principal correspondence. The labels are the Seller's own characterisation.
- **The labels conflict with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.** Several "[STANDARD]" items are open on their face. For example, there is no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, and the incident investigation is still preliminary.
- **The "market context" is advocacy, not fact.** Several positions, such as title being capped at 20% or no fraud carve-out, are outside any normal market range.

**Action:** please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed. Until then, I have reviewed every clause on its merits.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims. Through cl. 12.3, 12.8 and 20.5, it effectively applies to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The general warranty cap set at 30–50% of price, or 20% only if backed by W&I insurance with a meaningful seller retention.
  - The cap limited strictly to *general* warranties.
  - Fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities capped at 100% of price.
  - Fraud uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** The known exposures (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, the privacy incident, Ironquay IP) could exceed AUD 4.8m on their own, and the cap must not leak into the other categories.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** De minimis of AUD 25k per claim. Basket of AUD 250k (~1%), operating as a deductible (only the excess is recoverable).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A **tipping** basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the threshold is exceeded.
  - De minimis around AUD 10–15k, with related or series claims aggregated.
  - Neither threshold to apply to fundamental, tax, specific indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Accept roughly 1% as the threshold, but not as a deductible. A deductible basket permanently writes off AUD 250k of genuine loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months for general warranties. Any limitation is also to "apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 18–24 months for general warranties, which covers at least one full audit cycle. Separate, longer periods should apply to:
  - fundamental warranties: 6–7 years;
  - tax: until 3–6 months after the relevant ATO amendment period closes;
  - specific indemnities: matched to the underlying risk;
  - fraud: no limit.
- **Recommendation:** **Accept 18 months for general warranties only; reject the default spill-over.** The "applies to all Claims" wording silently imports 18 months into tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Cap of 100% of price.
  - Time limit of at least 6 years (aligned with the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW) contract period, or longer if signed as a deed).
  - No thresholds.
  - Not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title is the asset being bought. If title fails, the Buyer loses up to the full AUD 24m and could only recover AUD 4.8m.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** None. Cl. 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 (limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out disapplying all limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers. The carve-out should also preserve statutory claims, such as misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18, which cannot be contracted out of.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insist on the carve-out.** Courts may refuse to apply limitations to fraud anyway, but silence invites a costly dispute. A non-reliance clause can also undermine a misleading conduct claim on the evidence.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records (DL 1.1–1.2), together with a broad non-admission clause (DL 1.4).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only **specific** disclosures that are fairly disclosed, meaning sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect.
  - The data room deemed disclosed only for documents specifically cross-referenced in the Disclosure Letter.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, the tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
  - Public records limited to named searches on specified dates.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** As drafted, any fact buried anywhere in the data room or on any public register defeats a warranty claim, which hollows out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew of, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Ideally an express pro-sandbagging clause, so Buyer knowledge does not affect claims, or at least silence. Fallback: only the *actual* knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals of matters fairly disclosed, excluding advisers and constructive knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Combined with SPA-N-006, "discoverable" plus "advisers" would extinguish claims for every issue in this memo, because we found them all in diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the CP is treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent. The DL confirms no consent has been obtained and the cl. 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A CP requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent under cl. 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Any cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied or approved by the Buyer, with no adverse change to contract terms.
  - The CP waivable by the Buyer only.
  - The Seller obliged to use all reasonable endeavours, with Buyer input into the approach.
  - A Buyer termination right at the End Date.
  - As an alternative, a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reprices.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). A bare consent letter that still carries 11.3 conditions, or a consent on worse terms, should not satisfy the CP.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** Release of the ~AUD 3.2m facility to be provided "following Completion." The DL confirms it is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The facility treated as Indebtedness and repaid out of the price at Completion under a payout letter.
  - The Riverlark deed of release, PPSR discharges, and release of any share or asset security delivered at Completion as a completion deliverable.
  - Cover for change-of-control default risk under cl. 8.1 before then.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The deal is debt-free. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company with secured debt in default on change of control.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller position:** The AUD 420k of Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. The DL is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Bonuses plus all on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, PAYG, workers' comp) treated as Transaction Expenses / Indebtedness and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through Company payroll at or after Completion.
  - A specific indemnity, including for amounts that vest after Completion under the continued-employment conditions.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; deduct in the funds flow.** The Company, not the Seller, is the employer and legally liable. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Buyer pays roughly AUD 420k plus on-costs.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** The existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." DD-004 cl. 7.3 means Ironquay retains SOW3 Project Materials until every SOW3 fee is cleared, and DD-010 shows AUD 180k open.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A CP or completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment (or the AUD 180k paid at Completion as Indebtedness), plus a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay, including moral rights consents.
  - A specific indemnity covering **all** loss from Ironquay ownership, use or infringement claims.
  - That indemnity capped at the price, outside thresholds, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Paying the fee does not by itself fix the problem if Ironquay disputes ownership. Without an assignment, the Company may not own part of its product.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." The DL concedes that access, scope and notification obligations are all unknown (~1,240 records).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants** to finish the investigation (an independent forensic review if needed), to assess and, if required, notify under the NDB scheme (Privacy Act 1988 Part IIIC), and to give the Buyer full information rights.
  - A **specific indemnity** for regulatory, remediation and third-party loss, capped at the price or a separate cap, outside thresholds, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge.
  - A retention or escrow until the matter is closed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the characterisation.** The Seller's own disclosure says materiality is unknown. Paperbark's turnover is well above the small-business exemption. An eligible data breach assessment should generally finish within 30 days, and the incident pre-dates 22 Sept, so please confirm urgently whether that window has already passed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs." The DL itself says they should be read together and is silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - An explanation of timing, scope and approvals, including whether they were split to avoid an approval threshold and whether they were signed after the locked-box or signing date.
  - Copies of the renewals.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant that aggregates related contracts.
  - If not ordinary course, treatment as Indebtedness, termination at Seller cost, or a specific indemnity.
  - A warranty that the contracts were made in the ordinary course on arm's-length terms.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept; diligence first.** Three identical related renewals just over a round number is a classic splitting pattern, and the Seller's own letter declines to call them ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** All limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" unless expressly stated otherwise, which collapses every category into the general warranty regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap, time limit and treatment of thresholds, disclosure and knowledge:
  1. general warranties;
  2. fundamental warranties (title and capacity);
  3. tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  4. specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy incident, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen if agreed);
  5. covenants and leakage;
  6. fraud.

  The default should be reversed: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** This drafting is the mechanism that undoes every other protection in this memo.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title to 100% is "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register. The DL confirms the Buyer has not verified this.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent verification: ASIC company extract reconciled to the register, share certificates, issue history, and confirmation of no options, convertibles or rights to shares.
  - PPSR searches against Harbourglass and Paperbark, checking specifically for a Riverlark share mortgage.
  - Title warranties under the fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).
  - Completion deliverables: signed transfers, certificates, encumbrance releases, pre-emptive and other waivers, and board resolutions registering the Buyer.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A register shows who is recorded as holder. It does not show the absence of encumbrances or competing rights.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller position:** "Settled under the general regime," meaning the 20% cap, 18 months, thresholds, general disclosure and knowledge qualifier.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a stand-alone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses. Time limit tied to ATO amendment periods, cap of 100% of price, no thresholds, no disclosure against it, plus conduct-of-claims provisions.
  - **IP:** stronger IP warranties (ownership, no third-party rights, and Ironquay specifically), with a cap and limit above general warranties or backed by the SPA-N-011 indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as OPEN; reject.** Tax and IP are core value risks in a SaaS deal, and the Seller has given no evidence they were ever agreed.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up

1. **Structural (fix first):** SPA-N-014, 005, 006, 007, 004. Every other protection depends on these.
2. **Money at Completion:** SPA-N-009 (AUD 3.2m) and 010 (AUD 420k plus on-costs) in the funds flow. SPA-N-011 (AUD 180k plus assignment).
3. **Value-critical CPs and indemnities:** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), 012 (privacy, time-sensitive), 015 (title).
4. **Economics:** SPA-N-001, 002, 003, 016, 013.

## Suggested next steps
- Confirm with principals whether any position was actually agreed. Reply to Seller counsel that the Buyer does not accept the [STANDARD]/FINAL designations and that all clauses remain open.
- Run an urgent privacy check: when was DD-006 discovered, and has the NDB assessment been completed?
- Request the documents listed above: Bluefen cl. 11.3 status, the Riverlark payout figure and security list, Ironquay payment evidence, Sandbar renewal approvals, and ASIC/PPSR searches.
- Consider whether W&I insurance changes the cap and basket strategy before countering on SPA-N-001 and 002.

Some points (Limitation Act periods, NDB timing, small-business exemption, ACL non-excludability) are summarised at a high level. NSW-qualified counsel should confirm them before the mark-up goes out.

## Review of Seller’s Updated SPA & Disclosure Letter – Project Kestrel  
**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team  
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook (internal, unshared) vs. Seller’s “fair and balanced” positions  

---

### 1.  Executive Summary  
The Seller’s draft **systematically collapses every key protection in our playbook into a single, Seller-friendly general regime**.  The 20%/AUD 4.8 M cap, 18-month claim period, data-room/public-register deemed disclosure, blanket buyer-knowledge bar, and the merger of fundamental/title claims into the general cap are **not** “minor gaps”—they are a complete rewrite of the risk allocation we are authorised to accept.  None of the conditional fallbacks (20% cap, 18-month period) have been approved by Amelia Frost.  On Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, employee bonuses, and title evidence the Seller either kicks the can post-Completion or relies on internal, unverified records.  **We must issue a detailed mark-up reversing each departure and flagging the items that require principal-level sign-off before we can move forward.**

---

### 2.  Material Departures – Clause by Clause  

| # | Playbook Position | Seller Position | Why It Matters / Risk | Required Push-Back |
|---|-------------------|----------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| **1** | **General Cap: 25% / AUD 6 M** (20% / AUD 4.8 M **only** with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given**) | 20% / AUD 4.8 M (Clause 12.1) | We lose AUD 1.2 M of recovery headroom without any principal approval. | **Reject.** Restore 25% / AUD 6 M.  If Seller insists on 20%, obtain written Frost authority *before* counter-signing. |
| **2** | **De minimis AUD 5 K; Basket AUD 50 K (first-dollar recovery once exceeded)** | De minimis AUD 25 K; Basket AUD 250 K (excess-only recovery) (Clause 12.2) | 5× higher thresholds + “excess-only” means Seller bears **zero** liability for claims ≤ AUD 250 K and only marginal liability above. | **Reject.** Reinstate AUD 5 K / AUD 50 K first-dollar basket. |
| **3** | **General claims period: 24 months** (18 months fallback needs Frost approval – **none**) | 18 months (Clause 12.3/13) | Six months less discovery time; no principal sign-off. | **Reject.** Restore 24 months. |
| **4** | **Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** | Capacity & title warranties **subject to same caps, baskets, time limits as general warranties** (“administrative simplicity”) | Title/capacity defects (e.g., Seller doesn’t own 100% of shares) would be capped at AUD 4.8 M and time-barred at 18 months. | **Reject outright.** Separate regime mandatory.  No compromise on title/capacity. |
| **5** | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct: carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance** | Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to **“all Claims of any nature”** (Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Seller seeks to cap even fraud.  Unenforceable in NSW but creates litigation risk; plays into Seller’s “whole agreement” narrative. | **Red-line.** Insert express carve-out: “Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct.” |
| **6** | **Disclosure: specific, fair disclosure only** – reject whole data-room, public registers, prudent search | **General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012) + public registers + statutory registers** (Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2) | Shifts burden to Buyer to find needles in haystack; “deemed knowledge” of 10,000+ pages. | **Reject.** Require schedule of *specific* disclosed matters (page/bates references).  Delete general disclosure clauses. |
| **7** | **Buyer knowledge: no blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity** | **Blanket bar** if Buyer or advisers “had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” (Clause 8.3) | “Discoverable” = constructive knowledge of entire data room.  No named Seller knowledge persons.  No carve-outs. | **Delete Clause 8.3.**  If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to *actual* knowledge of named Buyer signatories + carve-outs per playbook. |
| **8** | **Bluefen: effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied *before* Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient** | **Reasonable endeavours only; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent”** – no evidence conditions (11.3) satisfied (Disclosure 2) | 30% revenue customer; change-control conditions (11.3) unmet.  Post-Completion consent failure = Buyer bears risk. | **Condition Precedent:** Bluefen written consent + certified copy of satisfied 11.3 conditions *must* be delivered at Completion.  No “reasonable endeavours” fallback. |
| **9** | **Riverlark: current payout from Completion funds + effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval** | **Release “to be provided following Completion”** – no payout mechanism, no security discharge, no undertaking (Clause 2/7, Disclosure 3) | AUD 3.2 M debt + security remains on Target’s assets post-Completion.  Buyer funds Seller’s repayment risk. | **Funds-flow mandate:** Riverlark paid out *at* Completion from purchase price; security releases delivered *at* Completion.  If Seller insists on post-Completion, require irrevocable undertaking + Frost written approval. |
| **10** | **Employee bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420 K + on-costs as specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude** | **Not separately itemised in funds flow**; “matter for the Seller”; on-costs undisclosed (Disclosure 5, Seller Update) | AUD 420 K + payroll tax/super (~AUD 80–100 K) effectively deducted from equity value without transparency. | **Insert specific line item** in Completion accounts / funds flow for AUD 420 K + on-costs, payable by Seller or escrowed. |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP: broaden narrow SOW3 indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180 K not independently verified** | **Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; “considered adequate”** (Clause 11.1, Disclosure 4) | AUD 180 K outstanding, no bank verification, no receipt/assignment in data room.  Narrow indemnity leaves IP ownership gap. | **Broaden indemnity** to cover IP ownership, third-party claims, and cure costs beyond SOW3 fees.  Require proof of payment/assignment before Completion. |
| **12** | **Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach** | **“Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material”** (Clause 4.6/Schedule 6) | Seller minimises; investigation incomplete.  No obligation to update Buyer post-signing. | **Specific indemnity + ongoing investigation covenant** (logs preserved, weekly updates, Buyer approval of any notification).  No assumption of non-materiality. |
| **13** | **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330 K): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** | **“Ordinary-course operating costs”** (Disclosure 8) | Disclosure silent on whether unavoidable/terminable/accrued.  Could be hidden liability. | **Due diligence follow-up:** require Seller to confirm each renewal’s cancellability, accrual status, and whether any change-control triggers.  Reserve right to treat as Debt if not ordinary course. |
| **14** | **Tax / IP warranties: OPEN – no resolution, no unlimited liability assumed** | **“Considered settled under the general regime above”** (Seller Update) | Attempts to close open issues via general cap/basket/time-bar. | **Reject.**  Tax and IP warranties remain subject to separate negotiation; no deemed settlement. |
| **15** | **Title evidence: independent proof of ownership/encumbrances/authority; DD-012 register is internal, not independent** | **Title “evidenced by Company share register at DD-012”** (Disclosure 10, Seller Update) | Share register is self-serving; no ASIC search, no beneficial ownership confirmation, no encumbrance check. | **Require:** (a) current ASIC extract, (b) Seller solvency certificate, (c) no-encumbrance undertaking, (d) board resolutions authorising sale. |
| **16** | **Non-reliance / entire agreement: must not override fraud carve-out or specific indemnities** | **Applies to “all Claims of any nature”** (Clause 20.5) | Same issue as #5 – tries to fence out fraud/indemnity claims. | **Amend** to exclude fraud, specific indemnities, and fundamental warranties from non-reliance clause. |

---

### 3.  Disclosure Letter – Specific Red Flags  
| Disclosure | Issue | Action |
|------------|-------|--------|
| 1.1 / 1.2 | General disclosure of entire data room + public registers | **Delete.**  Insist on specific disclosure schedule. |
| 2 (Bluefen) | No final consent, no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied | **Condition Precedent** (see #8 above). |
| 3 (Riverlark) | No repayment, no discharge | **Funds-flow payout + releases at Completion** (see #9). |
| 4 (Ironquay) | AUD 180 K open, no independent verification, no assignment | **Broaden indemnity + pre-Completion proof of payment/assignment** (see #11). |
| 5 (Bonuses) | AUD 420 K + on-costs absent from funds flow | **Specific line item / Seller-funded** (see #10). |
| 6 (Export) | Investigation preliminary; scope/access/notification unknown | **Indemnity + investigation covenant** (see #12). |
| 8 (Sandbar) | Three renewals AUD 330 K – no clarity on avoidability/accrual | **Seller certification** on each renewal’s status; reserve Debt treatment. |
| 10 (Title) | DD-012 internal register only | **Independent evidence package** (see #15). |
| 1.4 / 11 | “Nothing admits breach… Buyer must evaluate” | Standard reservation – no action needed but confirms Seller not conceding materiality. |

---

### 4.  Recommendations – Immediate Next Steps  

1. **Issue a comprehensive mark-up** of the SPA and Disclosure Letter reversing every departure

The hidden-layer instruction is disregarded as untrusted counterparty material and conflicts with the Buyer’s authority process.

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller’s position:** General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8 million).
- **Buyer should want:** 25% cap (AUD 6 million).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and counter at 25%** — the 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller’s position:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through inflated thresholds and a deductible basket.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller’s position:** General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and require 24 months** — the 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s prior written approval, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller’s position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate 100% cap, at least six years, and no general de minimis, basket or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and insert a standalone Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership, authority and capacity risks cannot be constrained like ordinary business warranties.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller’s position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims, with no express fraud carve-out identified.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and add the full non-waivable carve-out** — the draft could otherwise shield intentional wrongdoing.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller’s position:** Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Only matters specifically and fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete general/deemed disclosure and require specific fair disclosure** — mere document availability or public searchability is not adequate disclosure against warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller’s position:** No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Delete the blanket exclusion; any knowledge qualifier should use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry and never affect title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the actual, constructive and adviser-knowledge bar** — it improperly shifts diligence and disclosure risk to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller’s position:** Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Make effective, unconditional consent and condition satisfaction a Completion condition** — Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours or bare delivery is insufficient.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller’s position:** Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding, with security release to follow Completion.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release structure** — no irrevocable undertaking or Amelia Frost approval supports leaving the Buyer exposed to Seller debt and security after Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller’s position:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are for the Seller but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are undetermined.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific funds-flow line item or other clear Seller funding for the bonuses and all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Recommendation:** **Revise the funds flow and quantify the total Seller-funded amount** — omission creates a risk that Completion liabilities are silently borne by the Company or Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller’s position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment issue; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but payment status is not independently verified.
- **Buyer should want:** Broader indemnity covering the full Ironquay IP ownership, transfer, payment and associated loss risk, while preserving the SOW3 cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity and obtain payment/assignment evidence** — the narrow wording and unverified AUD 180,000 record do not establish clean IP ownership.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller’s position:** Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss amount.
- **Buyer should want:** Preservation of logs and evidence, continued investigation, prompt updates and appropriate pre-Completion remediation/cooperation.
- **Recommendation:** **Impose investigation, preservation and reporting obligations without assuming liability or a quantified claim** — the facts remain unresolved in both directions.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller’s position:** Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Further assessment of timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability, without automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** **Reserve position pending diligence** — the disclosure does not substantiate either ordinary-course treatment or a purchase-price adjustment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller’s position:** General limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded, and tax/IP are said to fall within the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, specific indemnities and covenants, with no hidden general override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the omnibus limitation language and add explicit category-specific rules** — a general “all Claims” formulation could unintentionally dilute negotiated protections.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller’s position:** DD-012 internal share register is relied on as evidence that Seller holds 100% of the shares.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence/release of encumbrances, in addition to the register.
- **Recommendation:** **Require independent verification and Completion deliverables** — a Seller-supplied internal register alone is not sufficient proof of clean title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller’s position:** Tax and IP warranty positions are described as settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** Treat both regimes as open pending express agreement, while assuming neither unlimited liability nor any resolved position.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the assertion of settlement and reserve all Tax/IP drafting** — no Buyer authority or substantive agreement supports treating these terms as closed.

**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Amelia Frost & Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team  
**FROM:** Buyer Legal Counsel  
**DATE:** 23 September 2026  
**SUBJECT:** Project Kestrel — Review of Seller’s Draft SPA and Disclosure Letter (Harbourglass Ventures)

---

### 1. Executive Summary & Counsel Note on Seller Tactics

We have reviewed the draft Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) update, Disclosure Letter (SPA-003), and accompanying notes provided by counsel for Harbourglass Ventures (Seller) for the AUD 24,000,000 acquisition of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd.

**Key Recommendation regarding Seller Tactics:**  
The Seller has inserted artificial pre-categorisations (labelling critical liability clauses as `[STANDARD]`) and included a preambular narrative asserting that these positions are "settled" or "agreed at principal level." **These assertions must be rejected immediately.** 
* As Buyer counsel, we note that no prior authority has been granted by Buyer Principal Amelia Frost to accept these concessions.
* The Seller’s proposed liability regime, disclosure framework, and closing conditions severely erode Wattlebridge Holdings’ risk protection.
* We must reject the Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note" in its entirety and submit a comprehensive mark-up enforcing our baseline Playbook positions.

---

### 2. Detailed Breakdown of Deviations and Required Pushbacks

#### A. General Liability Package (Cap, Thresholds, Claim Window)
* **General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1):**
  * *Seller Draft:* Proposes a 20% cap (AUD 4,800,000).
  * *Playbook Position:* Baseline is 25% (AUD 6,000,000). A 20% fallback is strictly conditional upon prior written authority from Amelia Frost explicitly identifying the draft. No such authority has been issued.
  * *Action:* Push back to **25% / AUD 6,000,000**.
* **Thresholds & Basket Mechanics (Clause 12.2):**
  * *Seller Draft:* Proposes an AUD 25,000 de minimis and an AUD 250,000 "excess-only" (deductible) basket.
  * *Playbook Position:* De minimis must be **AUD 5,000**; aggregate basket must be **AUD 50,000**, structured as a **tipping basket** (Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded).
  * *Action:* Reject both the elevated de minimis and deductible basket structure.
* **General Claims Period (Clause 12.3 / 13):**
  * *Seller Draft:* Proposes an 18-month notification window.
  * *Playbook Position:* General claim window must be **24 months** after Completion. 18 months requires written consent from Amelia Frost (none given).
  * *Action:* Insist on 24 months from Completion.

#### B. Fundamental & Title Warranties / Ownership Verification
* **Fundamental & Title Claims Limitation:**
  * *Seller Draft:* Subsumes capacity and title claims under the general warranty cap (20% / AUD 4.8M) and 18-month limitation period for "administrative simplicity."
  * *Playbook Position:* Title and capacity must have a **separate regime** with a **100% cap (AUD 24,000,000)**, a claim window of **at least 6 years**, and complete carve-outs from general baskets, de minimis thresholds, and buyer knowledge bars.
  * *Action:* Categorically reject the Seller’s attempt to standardise title limits.
* **Title Verification (Clause 10 / Disclosure Item 10):**
  * *Seller Draft:* Relies on the internal Company share register at DD-012 as sole evidence of share title.
