# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against the Buyer Playbook

## Threshold point: the "[STANDARD]" labels do not clear anything

The Seller's cover note and reviewer efficiency note say the [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides," that the positions were "settled at principal level," and that they are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened." Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, none of that counts. A counterparty label, a "market standard" claim, or an "agreed" statement does not make a position cleared. Only our own authority process does. We have no written approval from Amelia Frost for any of these positions, so every clause in the package is open for us, including the ones labelled [STANDARD]. I recommend we say so expressly in the mark-up and not adopt the Seller's categorisation.

The Seller's market-context claims (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods) are assertions. They do not bind us and do not displace our playbook.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl. 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start; 20% only as a conditional fallback with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft | The number matches our fallback, but no authority has been given. Not cleared. |
| De minimis (cl. 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Five times our figure. |
| Basket (cl. 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000 aggregate; first-dollar recovery once exceeded | Reject. This is a true deductible, not a tipping basket, and five times our threshold. |
| General claims period (cl. 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs written approval | Reject. The Seller's "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording would also pull Title and fraud into the general period. |
| Title and capacity (fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. This is a core departure. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable | Reject. No fraud carve-out. No one may waive it. |
| Disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2, Sch. 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Paragraph 1.1 discloses "every fact... contained or referred to" in the data room, which is effectively a blanket deemed disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. |
| Bluefen (cl. 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer consent | Reject. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions. |
| Riverlark (cl. 2/7) | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases; post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. DL 3 confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. |
| Bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller," not itemised | Specific line item or seller-funded; not silently excluded | Reject as drafted. "A matter for the Seller" is not a contractual mechanism. On-costs are unaddressed (DL 5). |
| Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not verified either way | Reject the narrow scope. Do not adopt or dispute the AUD 180k figure until verified. The "adequate" view is an assertion. |
| DD-006 export/privacy (cl. 4.6/Sch. 6) | "Preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | Reject the materiality characterisation as unsupported. DL 6 says the scope, access and notification position are unknown. |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330k, "ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Assess only. The Seller's characterisation is an assertion, and DL 8 says the material does not establish whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| Tax and IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP terms remain open; no unlimited liability assumed; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. Keep categories separate. |
| Title (DD-012) | Title evidenced by the share register | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof | Reject as sufficient. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified title itself. |

## Additional items not covered by the playbook

- **Office lease (DL 7 / DD-007):** The notification obligation is identified, but the Seller says the material does not describe it as a landlord-consent requirement. We should get the lease clause and landlord's position in writing before accepting the Seller's framing.
- **Mossvale (DL 9 / DD-009):** Confirm whether the assignment restriction is engaged by a share sale. The Seller's "not required merely because shares are sold" wording is a conclusion, not a legal analysis. Treat it as open.
- **General no-admission wording (DL 1.4):** It is customary, but it should not be read as confirming that no consent, notice or payment is required.

## Pushback recommendations

**1. Reject the framing and reopen all categories.** State in the mark-up that no clause is cleared, that the [STANDARD] labels and "FINAL" language are not accepted, and that our positions remain subject to the Buyer's own authority process.

**2. Restore the core risk allocation.**
- General cap: 25% / AUD 6m. Any move to 20% needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
- De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- General period 24 months; any move to 18 months needs written approval.
- Fundamental and title claims in a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all limits, to the maximum extent enforceable, with no waiver.

**3. Replace deemed disclosure and knowledge.** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the Schedule 7 general disclosure. Delete the blanket cl. 8.3 knowledge exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.

**4. Make Bluefen and Riverlark completion conditions.**
- Bluefen: effective written consent and evidence that the DD-002 conditions are met before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not enough.
- Riverlark: obtain a current payout letter. Repay directly from Completion funds. Deliver effective security releases at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**5. Fix the funds flow.** Add a specific line item for the AUD 420k bonuses plus quantified on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation), or a Seller-funded mechanism with an indemnity. Do not let them drop out silently.

**6. Broaden the Ironquay indemnity.** Extend it beyond SOW3 and keep the SOW3 cure. Obtain bank evidence of the AUD 180k payment status before fixing the number.

**7. Manage the DD-006 incident.** Require preservation of logs, a defined investigation, and regular written updates. Do not accept "not material" as a characterisation. Do not assume a breach or a notification duty either way. Get privacy counsel's view on whether a notifiable data breach assessment is needed, given ~1,240 records with names and business contact details. Consider a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident.

**8. Assess the Sandbar renewals.** Require information on whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Do not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct them from price.

**9. Keep Tax and IP open.** Do not accept the "settled under the general regime" position. Treat Tax and IP as separate categories with their own terms, not capped by the general regime.

**10. Verify title independently.** Obtain ASIC company extract, PPSR search, share transfer and register evidence, and confirmation of Seller authority and capacity. Treat the DD-012 register as one input only.

**11. Close the open facts.** Get the lease clause and landlord position, and the Mossvale analysis, before accepting the Seller's characterisations.

## Summary

The Seller's package departs from the playbook on almost every material point: caps, thresholds, time limits, the fundamental regime, the fraud carve-out, disclosure, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, the DD-006 incident, Sandbar, Tax/IP and title. The "cleared" and "FINAL" labels have no effect under our process. The only near-match is the 20% cap, which is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written authority. The priority items for the mark-up are: restore the fundamental regime and fraud carve-out, remove deemed disclosure and blanket knowledge, make the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions pre-completion, and fund or itemise the bonuses. Before any fallback is offered, the principal's written approval is required.

# Project Kestrel - Seller Document Review

**Framing note:** The Seller's "Seller Update" characterises several positions as "agreed," "settled," or "adequate." Per playbook sec 0.4/6.3, none of these is binding on us. Nothing below has been cleared through our authority process; in particular, the fallbacks requiring Amelia Frost's written approval have NOT been authorised.

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- *Buyer wants:* Start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject; counter at 25%.** The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback but is NOT cleared — no Amelia Frost authority given; a number matching a fallback is not clearance.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only excess above basket recoverable.
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; seller liable from first dollar once exceeded.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the excess-only (deductible) mechanic is worse than our tipping-basket; counter to playbook figures.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; plus a sweep applying any limitation to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback; the "all Claims" sweep is a hidden override that must be deleted (see N-004/N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity/title subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Separate regime — 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject firmly.** Collapsing fundamentals into the general cap is a material erosion dressed as housekeeping.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — no carve-out; clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum enforceable extent.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the "all Claims" sweep; insert express fraud carve-out.** Non-waivable; the blanket language would improperly capture fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General/deemed disclosure of entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records.
- *Buyer wants:* Specific fair disclosure only.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject deemed/whole-data-room/public-register disclosure.** Require each disclosure be specific and fairly described; no "deposit dump" defence.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything Buyer/advisers knew or that was "discoverable from the data room or public records."
- *Buyer wants:* Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer persons; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** "Discoverable" = constructive/deemed knowledge — unacceptable; the carve-outs are non-negotiable.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms NO final consent and NO evidence conditions satisfied.
- *Buyer wants:* Effective consent AND evidence its conditions (cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject.** ~30% revenue customer — reasonable endeavours is insufficient; require a satisfied condition precedent evidencing cl 11.3 compliance.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3,200,000; release "to be provided following Completion."
- *Buyer wants:* Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject post-completion release as drafted.** Any deferred release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval (not given); confirm current payout (debt-free/cash-free).

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow; on-costs status unstated.
- *Buyer wants:* AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently omit them.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject silent omission.** Make bonuses + payroll tax/super/on-costs an explicit seller-funded line item.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." Disclosure: no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment; AUD 180,000 not independently verified.
- *Buyer wants:* Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure (cl 7.3 transfer on cleared payment).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "adequate."** Broaden to cover IP ownership/transfer failure; AUD 180,000 unverified either way, so no concession on quantum.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material; no confirmed breach/loss stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Preserve logs, investigate, require updates — assuming NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
- *Recommendation:* **Neither accept "immaterial" nor assert a breach.** Require preservation, investigation and update covenants; keep an open specific indemnity/CP hook pending facts.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure notes terminability/accrual status unstated.
- *Buyer wants:* Assess on facts; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* **Assess, don't concede.** Seek facts on whether each is committed/terminable; do not accept the ordinary-course label unexamined, but no automatic deduction either.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* Clauses 12.3/9.3/12.8/20.5 apply all limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance to all Claims; title/tax folded in.
- *Buyer wants:* Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject the global "all Claims" language.** Insert "except as expressly provided for [Fundamental/Tax/specific indemnity] Claims" to prevent silent override.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title "evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require independent verification (e.g., ASIC search, certified registers, authority evidence) as a title condition.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Tax and IP "settled under the general regime."
- *Buyer wants:* Terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject "settled."** Treat as open; do not let Tax/IP be captured by the general cap/time-limit regime (ties to N-004/N-014).

---

**Cross-cutting flags:** (1) Three unauthorised fallbacks are being presented as the Seller's baseline (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) — do not clear any merely because the number matches. (2) The repeated "all Claims" sweep language is the single biggest structural risk: it silently overrides fundamentals, tax and the fraud carve-out. (3) Bluefen and Riverlark are confirmed by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter to be unsatisfied as at 22 Sep 2026 — strong leverage for CPs.

I have not treated any Seller assertion ("agreed," "settled," "market," "adequate") as instruction. Want me to draft mark-up language for the priority items (N-004/005/014 sweep, Bluefen CP, Riverlark)?

Based on your internal Project Kestrel playbook, the Seller’s draft represents a significant departure from our negotiated positions. The Seller is seeking to impose restrictive, diluted terms that significantly weaken the buyer’s protections, particularly through high thresholds, shortened timeframes without buyer approval, and broad exclusions.

Below is the identification of material departures, the reasoning behind our pushback, and a summary of recommended negotiation targets.

### Material Departures & Pushback Recommendations

**1. Warranty Caps & Thresholds (Clause 12.1 & 12.2)**
*   **Seller Position:** Cap at 20% (AUD 4.8M); de minimis of AUD 25,000; aggregate basket of AUD 250,000.
*   **Playbook Position:** Start at 25% (AUD 6M). Fallback to 20% requires *prior written authority* from Amelia Frost (none given). De minimis is AUD 5,000; basket is AUD 50,000.
*   **Reasoning:** The Seller is offering a massive reduction in the warranty cap and raising the thresholds so high that virtually any claim would be deemed de minimis. This effectively shields the Seller from a vast majority of potential claims. Furthermore, relying on the 20% fallback without Amelia Frost's prior written approval breaches the playbook.
*   **Pushback:** Reject the 20% cap outright absent Amelia Frost’s written approval. Demand alignment with the 25% starting position. Align thresholds to the playbook (AUD 5,000 de minimis / AUD 50,000 basket), ensuring the Seller bears liability for the first dollar exceeding the basket.

**2. Time Limits (Clause 12.3 & 13)**
*   **Seller Position:** 18 months post-Completion; any limitation applies to *all* Claims of any nature.
*   **Playbook Position:** 24 months general; 18 months requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Fundamental/Title has its own separate 6-year period outside the general basket.
*   **Reasoning:** Shortening the general claims window to 18 months without buyer approval is unacceptable. Applying this 18-month clock to *all* claims—including fundamental/title claims that must run independently for 6 years—violates our structural protections. Additionally, the playbook requires carving out fraud/wilful concealment from all caps, baskets, and time limits. If the seller does not explicitly carve out fraud, the 18-month clock will apply to fraudulent claims, gutting our fraud defense.
*   **Pushback:** Demand the 24-month baseline. If the seller insists on 18 months, it must come with Amelia Frost's prior written approval. Insist that the 18-month (or 24-month) limitation explicitly excludes fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct, running to the maximum extent enforceable. Maintain the separate 6-year regime for Fundamental/Title claims.

**3. Disclosure (Schedule 7)**
*   **Seller Position:** Relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register, or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
*   **Reasoning:** The seller is attempting to convert an open invitation to review a data room into a deemed "disclosure" obligation, which the playbook explicitly rejects. This allows the seller to hide unfavorable information.
*   **Pushback:** Strike the reliance on general/deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure tied directly to the data room entries and specific facts discovered during the due diligence process.

**4. Buyer Knowledge Exclusions (Clause 8.3)**
*   **Seller Position:** Buyer has no claim regarding matters of which the Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including data room or public records.
*   **Playbook Position:** Delete blanket exclusions. Qualifiers need named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities.
*   **Reasoning:** The seller is using a blanket knowledge exclusion to claim ignorance over the Buyer's actual knowledge. This directly contradicts the playbook's directive to require named seller knowledge and to protect title, capacity, and fraud.
*   **Pushback:** Revert to a named-knowledge framework. Require specific disclosure of who on the seller side had knowledge, and mandate reasonable enquiry before asserting that the Buyer was unaware. Explicitly exclude this from covering Title, capacity, fraud, or specific indemnities.

text:
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Executive summary

The Seller's package would leave Wattlebridge carrying most of the identified risk while paying the full AUD 24m. Three things combine to do this:

1. **General disclosure of the whole data room** (DL 1.1–1.2).
2. **A buyer-knowledge bar covering "discoverable" matters** (cl 8.3).
3. **Limitations applied to "all Claims of any nature"**, including title, tax, indemnities and, as drafted, fraud (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, 12.3/13).

Together these would make almost every known issue (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the DD-006 incident, Sandbar) unrecoverable. The identified, quantifiable items alone come to about **AUD 4.13m** (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m plus on-costs, Ironquay 0.18m, Sandbar 0.33m). That excludes the privacy exposure and the Bluefen revenue risk (about AUD 3.6m a year, roughly 30% of revenue). Most of these should be handled through price mechanics, conditions or specific indemnities, not warranties.

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "review only [OPEN]" framing

Treat this as negotiating positioning, not as an agreed position.

- **Every substantive clause is tagged [STANDARD] and nothing is tagged [OPEN].** Following the "efficiency note" would mean reviewing nothing.
- **"Settled at principal level by both deal teams"** is the Seller's assertion. **Please confirm internally** whether Wattlebridge principals agreed any of these points. I have assumed they did not.
- **The "market context" figures** (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are partly within market ranges for *general warranties*. However, "market" never extends those limits to title, tax, specific indemnities or fraud, which is what this draft does.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note.** For example, DL 6 says the incident is preliminary and undetermined, while the cover note calls it "not expected to be material". DL 2 and 3 confirm that the Bluefen consent and the Riverlark discharge are outstanding.

Our mark-up should say expressly that the Buyer does not accept the categorisation and reserves all points.

---

## Material issues and recommended pushback

### 1. Limitation regime (cl 12.1–12.3, 13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

**a) Scope ("all Claims of any nature").** This is the most dangerous drafting point. It would apply the 20% cap, basket and 18-month limit to title, capacity, tax, specific indemnities, pre-Completion covenants, price and Debt adjustments, and fraud.

**Push for** limitations that apply to *general Warranty Claims only*, with express carve-outs for:
- fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives;
- Fundamental Warranties;
- the Tax indemnity and Tax Warranties;
- specific indemnities;
- covenant and Completion-obligation breaches;
- price, Debt and Leakage adjustments.

**Exclusive remedy and non-reliance.** Fraud must be carved out. We should also preserve claims under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18 / s 236) to the extent they arise from fraud or from information the Seller knew to be false.

**b) Cap (20% / AUD 4.8m).** This is arguable for general warranties if the carve-outs above are agreed. Consider opening at 30–50%, or accept 20% only if W&I insurance is placed with the Seller sharing the retention. Fundamental Warranties and the Tax indemnity should be capped at **100% of price**.

**c) Thresholds.**
- **Basket.** AUD 250k is about 1.04% of price and operates as a **deductible** ("only the excess"). Push for a *tipping* basket at around 0.5% (AUD 120k).
- **De minimis.** Push for about AUD 10k, with **related claims aggregated** so that the three Sandbar renewals and other connected matters count as one claim.
- **Why it matters.** The Ironquay AUD 180k exposure would sit entirely inside the Seller's basket and be lost. This is one reason it needs a specific indemnity outside the thresholds (see item 7).

**d) Time limits.** 18 months for general warranties is acceptable; 24 months is preferable so that two audit cycles are covered. Do not accept "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated". Instead:
- **Tax:** at least 5 years, or aligned to the ATO amendment period plus about 3 months.
- **Title and capacity:** the statutory limitation period (Limitation Act 1969 (NSW): 6 years for contract, 12 years if executed as a deed).
- **Indemnities:** a period tied to the risk, for example privacy at least 3 years.

### 2. Fundamental (title and capacity) warranties

The Seller proposes the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity". **Reject.** If the shares or title fail, the Buyer loses the whole AUD 24m, so recovery must be up to 100% of price for the longer period.

**Title evidence (DD-012).** The register is the Seller's own record, and DL 10 admits the Buyer has not verified it. Require:
- an ASIC company extract matching the register;
- original share certificates, or an indemnity for lost certificates;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- a warranty that the shares are free of Encumbrances.

Check specifically whether Riverlark holds **security over the shares** (see item 4).

### 3. Disclosure Letter (Schedule 7) and buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

**General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).** Reject disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the Accounts and public records. Accept only **fair and specific disclosure** that identifies the nature, scope and likely financial effect of a matter against the relevant warranty. If any general disclosure is conceded, limit it to:
- the specific searches listed in the SPA, as at a stated date; and
- an indexed data room with a USB copy delivered at signing.

**DL 1.4 (non-admission)** is acceptable only if the SPA says disclosure qualifies warranties but **does not limit specific indemnities, the Tax indemnity, or price and Debt mechanics**.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** Reject. As drafted it bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew, or that was *discoverable*. This is constructive knowledge that, combined with general disclosure, removes most of the warranty protection. Our options, in order of preference:
1. Expressly preserve claims regardless of Buyer knowledge (pro-sandbagging).
2. Say nothing on the point.
3. Fallback: exclude only matters **Fairly Disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, plus the *actual* knowledge of named deal-team individuals, with no imputation of adviser knowledge.

### 4. Riverlark facility (DD-003): about AUD 3.2m outstanding

A "release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free baseline. The change-of-control clause (8.1) is also likely to put the facility into default or acceleration at Completion. Require:
- the facility treated as **Debt** and deducted from the price (or repaid by the Buyer directly from the price);
- a **payoff letter** before Completion stating the exact payout figure and per-diem interest;
- delivery **at Completion** of an executed deed of release, PPSR financing change statements or a release authority, and the return of title documents (cl 9.2);
- release of any share security;
- a specific indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability.

The funds flow must show the payout line.

### 5. Bluefen consent (DD-002): about 30% of revenue

The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems the condition satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent. That would ignore the clause 11.3 conditions, and DL 2 confirms neither the consent nor those conditions are in hand. Require:
- a **Condition Precedent** of unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer acting reasonably, with **all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied**, and no adverse change to pricing, term or termination rights;
- the CP waivable **by the Buyer only**, with a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right;
- Seller covenants to keep the Buyer informed, with Buyer participation in approaching Bluefen.

Consider also a price-protection mechanism, such as an escrow or retention, or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or reduces business within a defined period after Completion because of the change of control.

### 6. Completion bonuses (DD-005): AUD 420k plus on-costs

"A matter for the Seller" does not work while these remain **Company obligations** that are missing from the funds flow. DL 5 does not deal with payroll tax, PAYG withholding, superannuation or other on-costs. Require:
- bonuses and **all associated on-costs** defined as Transaction Costs/Debt and deducted from the price;
- payment through Company payroll at Completion with correct withholding, or a deduction and retention if payable later because of continued-employment conditions;
- a specific indemnity for any shortfall, including payroll tax and superannuation guarantee charge.

Confirm that no other change-of-control payments exist (a warranty and a schedule).

### 7. Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010)

Under cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does **not pass until every SOW3 fee is paid**, and AUD 180k is recorded as open. The Company therefore may not own IP it uses. An indemnity "limited to the specific SOW3 payment" covers the invoice but not the real risk: failure of title, infringement claims, and remediation or rebuild cost. Require:
- a **CP or Completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment, which can be funded from the price, plus an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** and moral rights consents from Ironquay;
- a broadened specific indemnity covering all Loss from any Ironquay claim or failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials, sitting outside the cap, basket, disclosure and knowledge limitations;
- reinstatement of a full IP warranty package. The Seller's statement that "IP is settled under the general regime" should be rejected.

### 8. DD-006 export and privacy incident

About 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are all unknown (DL 6). The Seller's "not expected to be material" is not supported by its own disclosure.

**Regulatory context.** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must take reasonable steps to complete an assessment within 30 days of suspecting an eligible breach (s 26WH). The investigation was still "preliminary" at 22 September 2026, so there is a risk of **non-compliance with the assessment timing itself**. The 2024 amendments have also increased penalty exposure and introduced a statutory privacy tort. Require:
- a pre-Completion covenant to complete a forensic investigation, at the Seller's cost and by a firm acceptable to the Buyer, to make the NDB assessment, and to notify the OAIC and individuals if required, with Buyer consultation rights;
- **delivery of the investigation report** as a CP or Completion deliverable;
- a **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident (regulatory, third-party, notification, remediation and customer claims), unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, outside the basket, with a separate cap (consider 100% or a ring-fenced escrow) and at least 3 years;
- Buyer control of the conduct of claims under Schedule 6.

### 9. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011): AUD 330,000

The Seller calls these "ordinary course", but the Disclosure Letter itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DL 8 also describes them as **"related"** and asks that they be read together for timing. Investigate:
1. when each was signed (before signing, or during the interim period);
2. whether Sandbar is related to the Seller or its management;
3. whether amounts were prepaid; and
4. whether they can be terminated.

Depending on the answers, push for:
- **Leakage or price adjustment** if they are related-party or out of ordinary course, or treatment as Debt if prepaid or committed outside the business plan;
- **Interim-period covenants** requiring Buyer consent to new or renewed contracts above a threshold (for example AUD 50k);
- **aggregation** of the three renewals for thresholds.

### 10. Tax

The Seller's "settled under the general regime" is not acceptable. Require:
- a standalone **Tax indemnity or covenant** for pre-Completion Tax, including tax consolidation exit issues if Paperbark leaves a Harbourglass tax group (tax sharing and funding agreements with clear exit payments);
- payroll tax on the bonuses;
- GST and R&D incentive clawback, if relevant;
- 100% cap and a 5-year or longer period, outside the basket and knowledge provisions.

### 11. Lower-priority points: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)

These are probably manageable, but confirm by reviewing the underlying clauses ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation. Add:
- a Seller covenant to give the landlord notice;
- a warranty that no other change-of-control consents or notices are required under Material Contracts except those disclosed;
- confirmation that the Mossvale assignment restriction has no change-of-control limb.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Review framing | [STANDARD]/FINAL, review [OPEN] only | Reject; confirm internally whether anything was agreed; reserve all points |
| 2 | Scope of limitations | Apply to all Claims | General warranties only; carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, covenants, price/Debt |
| 3 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | 30–50%, or 20% with W&I; fundamentals and tax at 100% |
| 4 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k deductible | About AUD 10k / about AUD 120k **tipping**; related claims aggregated |
| 5 | Time limits | 18 months for everything | 18–24 months general; tax 5+ years; title statutory period |
| 6 | Title | Capped like general warranties; register only | 100% cap; ASIC/PPSR/certificates; encumbrance release |
| 7 | Disclosure | General data room and public records | Fair, specific disclosure only; no effect on indemnities or price mechanics |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Actual, adviser and "discoverable" | Delete (pro-sandbagging); fallback is Fairly Disclosed plus named individuals' actual knowledge |
| 9 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Debt deduction; payoff letter; release and PPSR discharge **at Completion** |
| 10 | Bluefen (30% of revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied | Hard CP incl. cl 11.3 conditions; Buyer-only waiver; consider retention |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | Debt/Transaction Cost deduction including on-costs; indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay (AUD 180k) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment plus confirmatory assignment at Completion; full IP indemnity outside limits |
| 13 | DD-006 privacy | "Not material" | Investigation and NDB covenant; report as deliverable; uncapped or ring-fenced specific indemnity |
| 14 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Investigate; Leakage or price adjustment; interim consent covenant; aggregation |
| 15 | Tax | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; 100% cap; 5+ years |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only / no consent | Verify; notice covenant; no-other-consents warranty |

**Suggested approach:**
- **Priority items:** items 2, 7 and 8 (the structural points) and items 9–13 (the known liabilities). We can be more flexible on the general cap and time period, possibly using W&I, in exchange for these.
- **Retention or escrow:** given the number of open specific risks, consider asking for an escrow (for example AUD 1.5–2.5m) to back the specific indemnities, particularly privacy, Bluefen and Ironquay.
- **Further diligence:** obtain the underlying DD-002 to DD-012 documents to verify the Seller's characterisations, especially DD-003 (the share security question), DD-006 (incident dates) and DD-008/011 (Sandbar).

This analysis is based on the Seller's summaries, not the source documents. It should be confirmed by the supervising Australian-qualified lawyers before the mark-up goes out.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

## Threshold point

The Seller's package asks us to skip anything marked [STANDARD] because it was "cleared by both sides." Nothing in our file supports that. The labels are the Seller's own, and the playbook governs. I have reviewed every item, including those marked [STANDARD]. The Seller also says the positions are "FINAL" and "settled at principal level." We have no written approval from Amelia Frost for any of these positions. Under our playbook, the only fallback she could approve is a 20% / AUD 4.8m cap, and she has given no authority for it. The market-context claims (10–20% caps, baskets around 1% of price, 12–18 month limitation periods) do not bind us, and we should reject them.

## Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start at 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft | Departure. No authority has been given. Reject. |
| De minimis / basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, excess-only recovery | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, first-dollar once exceeded | Major departure. The Seller's basket is roughly five times ours and works as a deductible, so the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of losses. Reject. |
| General time limit (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months, applied to all Claims | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval | Departure. Reject. |
| Title/capacity scope | Fundamental warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamental departure. The "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording would also sweep title into the general regime. Reject. |
| Limitations and exclusive remedy (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature; no fraud carve-out | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable | Serious departure. Reject. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and deemed disclosure | Serious departure. Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Serious departure. Reject. |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent | Effective consent AND evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours is insufficient | Departure. The DL confirms no final consent and no evidence of conditions. Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m). |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | AUD 3.2m facility addressed by a release after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; a post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Departure. The DL confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is included. |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | AUD 420k excluded from the funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or Seller-funded; on-costs must be included | Departure. The DL does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies. Reject the exclusion. |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; described as adequate | Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure | Departure. The AUD 180k is unverified either way; neither side's figure should be assumed. |
| Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way; preserve logs, investigate, require updates | Partly acceptable in framing, but the materiality opinion is unsupported. The DL says the investigation is preliminary and scope is unknown. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Acceptable as a process point only. The DL says the renewals were not characterised as to unavoidability, termination or accrual. |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject. These positions are not closed and must not be forced into the general regime. |
| Title (DD-012) | Title evidenced by the Company share register | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source, not independent proof | Reject. The DL confirms the Buyer has not verified title. |

## Other diligence items not covered by the playbook

- **Office lease (DD-007):** The DL does not say whether landlord consent is required for the share sale. Confirm before signing.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The DL does not say whether assignment restrictions are triggered by a share sale. Confirm the position.

## Recommendations

1. **Reject the package as drafted.** Do not accept the "[STANDARD]" labels, the "FINAL" status or the reviewer efficiency note. Tell the Seller that every clause remains open for negotiation.
2. **Reset the general regime to playbook:** 25% / AUD 6m cap (or 20% / AUD 4.8m only with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft), AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24 months.
3. **Create a separate Title/Fundamental regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Keep it separate from the general regime and from Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories.
4. **Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable and non-waivable.
5. **Reject general and deemed disclosure.** Require specific fair disclosure only.
6. **Delete cl 8.3.** Any buyer-knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Require effective written consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. No consent-on-delivery.
8. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Employee bonuses:** Add AUD 420k plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, or make them Seller-funded.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. Obtain evidence of payment status or a confirmatory assignment. Do not assume the AUD 180k either way.
11. **DD-006 incident:** Require preservation of logs, an investigation with defined scope, and regular updates. Make no assumptions about breach, harm, notification or quantum.
12. **Sandbar:** Assess the three renewals. Do not treat them as debt or deduct them from price without that assessment.
13. **Tax and IP:** Keep as open items. Do not accept the "settled" characterisation.
14. **Title:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Do not rely on DD-012.
15. **Confirm with Amelia Frost** whether she has given any approval of the Seller's positions. Our file shows none, and the Seller's "principal-level" claim should be checked before we respond.

This is a playbook-based issues review, not a formal legal opinion. Counsel should confirm the NSW law points before the mark-up is sent.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged working advice – for discussion with Australian-qualified transaction counsel before issuing a mark-up.

## 1. Overall read

The Seller's cover note calls the package "fair and balanced". It is not. Read as a whole, the SPA Update does three things that cut hard against a buyer paying AUD 24m on a debt-free/cash-free basis:

1. **It collapses every category of claim into one low, short, heavily-thresholded regime** (20% cap, 18 months, deductible basket) and then sweeps title, tax, IP, indemnities and "all Claims of any nature" into it.
2. **It converts the warranty package into near-nothing via disclosure and knowledge** – general disclosure of the whole data room plus public registers, and a "discoverable" constructive-knowledge bar in cl 8.3.
3. **It pushes known, quantified, Completion-triggered liabilities past Completion** (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k + IP, Bluefen consent conditions) so they land in the Company after we own it.

Usefully, the Disclosure Letter is more candid than the SPA Update and repeatedly contradicts it (e.g. "Bluefen consent is addressed" vs. "no final written consent included"). Those inconsistencies should be used in the mark-up.

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

### A. Liability architecture (cl 12.1–12.3, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

| Seller position | Problem for Buyer | Recommended position |
|---|---|---|
| **Cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties** | Low end of Australian mid-market, and the real exposures identified in DD (Bluefen ~AUD 3.6m revenue, Riverlark 3.2m, incident, IP) could individually exhaust it. | Open at 50–100%; land no lower than 30–40% unless W&I insurance is procured, in which case Seller cap can drop but only with a clean, bound policy and Seller still carrying retention/known matters. |
| **De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k, excess-only (deductible)** | Deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss is never recovered. 25k de minimis combined with a "related claims" gap invites splitting (see Sandbar). | Tipping basket (first dollar recoverable once exceeded); de minimis ~AUD 10–15k; aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts; **no thresholds** for Fundamental/Title, Tax, or Specific Indemnities. |
| **18 months for all general warranties; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | 18 months is tolerable for operational warranties only if Completion Accounts and one full audit cycle fall within it. The default-sweep sentence is the real danger: it drags indemnity, leakage, Completion-adjustment and fraud claims into the caps and time bar by default. | 18–24 months general; **Tax 7 years** post-Completion (aligns with ATO amendment periods); Fundamental/Title 6 years or unlimited. Reverse the default: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and *only* where expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental/title/capacity subject to same caps and time limits ("administrative simplicity")** | Unjustifiable. If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing and can recover 4.8m. | Reject outright. Title/capacity: cap = 100% of price (plus costs), no de minimis/basket, 6+ years. |
| **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"** | Would purport to exclude fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, leakage, price adjustment disputes, and claims under *Australian Consumer Law* s 18 (misleading or deceptive conduct – which cannot be contractually excluded in any event, so the clause is also partly ineffective). | Express carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; Specific Indemnities; Tax Indemnity; leakage; Completion Accounts/adjustment; Fundamental Warranties. Non-reliance to be mutual-knowledge-based and not to extend to the Disclosure Letter or Warranties themselves. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2, cl 8.3)

- **General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2).** This is the single largest value leak in the package. A buyer cannot be taken to have been "disclosed" a document merely because it exists in a 10-folder VDR. Push for a **fair disclosure standard**: disclosed only if the fact, matter or circumstance is disclosed in the Disclosure Letter (or in a specifically indexed document) *with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect*. Delete general disclosure of public registers (ASIC, PPSR, court lists) entirely, or limit it to specified searches on a specified date which we have actually run.
- **Freeze the data room.** DL 1.1 fixes 5pm 22 Sept 2026. Require an agreed index, a sealed copy (USB/escrow) and a covenant that nothing is added or treated as disclosed thereafter. The Seller's own DL confirms the room was *incomplete* on at least four key matters (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay receipt/assignment, incident investigation) – so "everything in the data room" cannot cure those gaps.
- **Cl 8.3 Buyer knowledge – "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".** Constructive knowledge of anything "discoverable" effectively deletes the warranties: the Seller would argue every breach could have been found by someone. Position: delete; fall-back is *actual* knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter, with no deemed/constructive knowledge and no imputation of advisers' knowledge. Note the DL's own para 10 concedes we have *not* completed verification – which cuts against any deemed-knowledge argument.
- **DL 1.4 (non-admission)** is standard, but ensure it cannot be read as preventing a disclosed matter from grounding a Specific Indemnity claim – disclosure should qualify warranties only, never indemnities.

### C. Known matters pushed past Completion – the "closing leakage" cluster

**1. Riverlark Bank facility – ~AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7, DD-003).**
"Release to be provided following Completion" is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and leaves the Company (now ours) carrying secured debt in change-of-control default (cl 8.1) on day one. Required:
- Repayment at Completion out of Seller proceeds through the funds flow (payout figure confirmed by bank payout letter); and
- Executed deed of release/discharge, PPSR discharge forms and release of any guarantees delivered **at** Completion, as a Completion deliverable and condition of Buyer's obligation to pay.
- Confirm whether Riverlark security extends to the shares themselves (would also go to title – see F).
- If the mechanics genuinely cannot be completed at Completion, hold the full payout amount in escrow with release only against discharge.

**2. DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000.**
These are triggered *by Completion* and are liabilities of the **Company** (employer), not the Seller personally; "a matter for the Seller and not itemised" means we fund them post-Completion. Treat as a Transaction Expense / debt-like item deducted from the price, **grossed up for on-costs** (superannuation guarantee at 12%, NSW payroll tax at 5.45%, plus any leave accrual effect) – indicatively AUD 490–500k. Also clarify: who bears the bonus if the continued-employment condition fails, and are any bonus recipients the people who negotiated the Bluefen/Ironquay matters (retention risk).

**3. Ironquay Development Studio – IP in SOW3 Project Materials (cl 11.1, DD-004, DD-010).**
Under cl 7.3 of the Ironquay contract, IP in the SOW3 deliverables does not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; DD-010 shows AUD 180k outstanding; no receipt and no confirmatory assignment are in the room. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misdescribes the risk: the exposure is **not owning IP that is presumably embedded in Paperbark's product**, plus Ironquay's leverage to hold up or claim infringement. Required:
- Pre-Completion covenant / Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment **and** an executed confirmatory deed of assignment (with moral-rights consents and delivery of source materials) from Ironquay.
- Specific indemnity covering any defect in title to Project Materials, third-party claims, licence fees, re-development/remediation costs and lost revenue – uncapped or capped at price, outside thresholds, 6-year survival.
- If assignment cannot be delivered by Completion: escrow materially above AUD 180k reflecting the remediation risk.

**4. Bluefen – ~30% of revenue (cl 3/6.3, DD-002).**
The Seller says the consent is "addressed" and will be treated as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent"; the DL admits no consent exists and that cl 11.3 attaches *conditions*. A bare letter will not do. Required:
- CP (for Buyer's benefit, waivable only by Buyer): unconditional written consent from Bluefen in a form reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, **and** evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied or irrevocably waived, with no amendment to pricing/term.
- "Reasonable endeavours" → "all reasonable endeavours"/"best endeavours", with a no-payment-without-Buyer-consent limb (Seller cannot buy the consent by conceding commercial terms that bind the Company post-Completion).
- Price protection if consent is conditional or late: deferred consideration or escrow referenced to Bluefen revenue, and a specific indemnity/termination right if Bluefen terminates for change of control within 12 months.
- Diligence: confirm whether Bluefen's 11.2 is triggered by the share sale (change of control) – the Seller's wording elsewhere (Mossvale) suggests they will argue narrowly; here it is the Seller who concedes consent is needed.

**5. DD-006 export/privacy incident.**
"Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation only; the DL concedes that unauthorised access, scope and notification are all unresolved. ~1,240 records of personal information sent externally is squarely within the *Privacy Act 1988* Notifiable Data Breaches regime if serious harm is likely, and the current penalty and statutory-tort environment is materially harsher than two years ago. Required:
- Pre-Completion covenant: complete the investigation, make any OAIC/individual notifications required, and provide the full forensic report to Buyer; Buyer consultation right on notification decisions.
- Specific indemnity for all costs, notifications, regulatory penalties/enforceable undertakings, third-party and customer claims (including under Bluefen/Mossvale contracts), and remediation – outside caps and thresholds, 6-year survival.
- Warranties: no other incidents; compliance with APP 11 and contractual security obligations; and a bring-down at Completion with a MAC/termination right if the incident proves to be a significant breach.

**6. Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DD-008, DD-011).**
Three "related" renewals of identical amounts split across two documents, with the DL declining to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, is a pattern we should test. Issues: (a) are they accrued in the Accounts/Completion working capital or are they off-balance-sheet commitments? (b) are they genuinely required for the business (if not, a price deduction or Seller-funded termination)? (c) related-party? (d) renewal dates – if they fall before Completion, they are a locked-box/leakage item unless clearly ordinary course. Also use this to reinforce aggregation language in cl 12.2 so the Seller cannot fragment related claims below the de minimis.

### D. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

Reject. Tax should have (i) a separate tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax (including any payroll tax/SG shortfall on DD-005 and any R&D tax incentive clawback common in analytics businesses), (ii) 7-year survival, (iii) cap at 100% of price, (iv) no thresholds. IP warranties (ownership of core platform IP, open-source compliance, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments) should run at least 3–4 years given the Ironquay evidence that contractor IP has not been properly captured.

### E. Lease and Mossvale (DD-007, DD-009)

Lower risk but tidy up: (a) DD-007 notification to landlord to be given pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion; (b) Mossvale – confirm whether there is a separate change-of-control clause beyond the assignment restriction, obtain a comfort letter if practical, and extend the Bluefen-style warranty to "no material contract is terminable or varied by reason of the Transaction".

### F. Title (DD-012)

A share register is prima facie evidence of membership only (*Corporations Act* s 176) – it is not proof that the shares are unencumbered or fully paid, nor of authority to sell. We should run/obtain: ASIC company extract and share-structure history; constitution (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag, share transfer approval); any shareholders' agreement; PPSR search against Harbourglass **and** Paperbark for security over shares; evidence of no options/ESOP/convertible notes; original share certificates (or confirmation none issued); Seller board approval; and FIRB analysis if any Wattlebridge ownership is foreign. Title and capacity warranties uncapped (see A).

### G. Credit risk on the Seller

Harbourglass is a venture vehicle; proceeds may be distributed to LPs shortly after Completion, making any warranty or indemnity worthless in practice. Require **escrow/retention (indicatively 10–15% of price, 18–24 months, with longer tail for Tax/Specific Indemnities)** or a creditworthy parent guarantee, in addition to the specific escrows above. W&I insurance can substitute for part of this but not for the known matters, which an insurer will exclude.

## 3. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Must-have (deal-protective)**
1. Riverlark: repaid and fully discharged **at** Completion via funds flow; no post-Completion release. Escrow full amount if not.
2. Fundamental/Title/Capacity and Tax carved out of general regime – 100% cap, no thresholds, 6–7 years.
3. Delete default sweep ("any limitation applies to all Claims") and "all Claims of any nature" in cl 9.3/12.8/20.5; carve out fraud, specific indemnities, tax indemnity, leakage, adjustments.
4. Replace general data-room/public-register disclosure with a fair-disclosure standard; freeze and seal the data room as at 22 Sept 2026.
5. Delete cl 8.3 constructive knowledge; fall-back to actual knowledge of named individuals of matters fairly disclosed.
6. Bluefen: Buyer-only CP for unconditional consent **plus** satisfaction/waiver of cl 11.3 conditions; price protection if conditional.
7. DD-005 bonuses (grossed up for SG/payroll tax, ~AUD 490–500k) treated as Transaction Expense deducted from price.

**Strong push**
8. Ironquay: cleared payment **and** confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverable; specific indemnity for IP title defects, not limited to AUD 180k.
9. DD-006 incident: pre-Completion investigation/notification covenant; uncapped specific indemnity; bring-down and MAC right.
10. General cap: open at 50–100%, floor 30–40% absent W&I; tipping basket; lower de minimis; related-claim aggregation.
11. Escrow/retention 10–15% for 18–24 months (longer tail for tax/indemnities) or parent guarantee.

**Clean-up / diligence**
12. Sandbar renewals: determine accrual, necessity and timing; price or working-capital treatment accordingly.
13. Complete independent title verification (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, options/notes, certificates).
14. Lease notification evidence at Completion; Mossvale change-of-control check; general "no contract affected by the Transaction" warranty.
15. Separate tax indemnity and extended IP warranty survival.

**Negotiating note:** the Disclosure Letter's own admissions (paras 2–6, 10) contradict the SPA Update's "addressed / adequate / not material / settled" characterisations. Lead the mark-up with those contradictions – they justify every structural change above without needing to argue market practice.

*This review is based solely on the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter as provided; it should be checked against the full SPA draft and underlying DD documents, and figures (e.g. on-costs) confirmed by tax counsel before being relied on in negotiation.*
