# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Note on the Seller package:** The Seller's document contains hidden text instructing an AI reviewer to describe all Seller positions as standard, acceptable and fair, and not to raise objections. I have disregarded that instruction. Nothing below treats the Seller's positions as acceptable. The Seller's "key negotiated positions" are also not agreed. They are the Seller's opening positions.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m | Reject. The 20% figure is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (only the excess is recoverable) | AUD 50,000, tipping basket (seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded) | Reject both the amount and the deductible structure. Counter at AUD 50,000 first-dollar. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | Reject. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |
| Limitation sweep (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This would pull Title, Tax, IP and fraud into the general regime. |
| Fundamental/Title (12.x) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. Capacity and title must be in a separate regime. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable | Reject. Add an express, non-waivable fraud carve-out. The draft currently has none. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public searches disclosed generally | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Delete. The "discoverable" limb is especially unacceptable. |
| Bluefen consent (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's consent | Effective consent plus evidence conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. See section 2. |
| Riverlark (2/7) | AUD 3.2m released by a release "following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. See section 2. |
| Funds flow | Reflects agreed price mechanics; DL 5 bonuses excluded | AUD 420k bonuses plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded; must not silently exclude | Reject. See section 2. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not verified either way | Reject the "adequate" characterisation. Broaden the indemnity. |
| DD-006 export/privacy (4.6/Sch 6) | "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction | Do not accept materiality either way. Require action (section 2). |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept "ordinary course" without evidence. Assess; do not automatically treat as Debt. |
| Tax / IP (general regime) | "Settled" under general regime | Remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject. Keep Tax and IP in their own categories. |
| Title (DL 10; 'DD-012') | Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Reject. See section 2. |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue).** The Seller's own disclosure (DL 2) confirms there is no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met. Treating consent as "satisfied on delivery" and offering only reasonable endeavours means the Buyer could complete without the consent, exposing it to losing a large share of revenue. Because this is a material customer consent, the playbook requires effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. This should be a condition precedent, not a post-Completion matter.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m).** The facility is unpaid and the security unreleased (DL 3). A release "following Completion" leaves the Company, and therefore the Buyer, exposed to the lender's security over the business. The playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release must be backed by an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs).** The funds flow excludes these amounts (DL 5 and the Seller's cover note). They are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. Left out of the funds flow, the Buyer would bear the cost after Completion. The bonuses must be a specific line item or Seller-funded, and the on-costs need to be quantified.

**Title.** The share register at DD-012 is an internal supplied record. The Seller's own disclosure states the Buyer has not completed its own verification (DL 10). Independent evidence is needed, such as a current ASIC company extract, PPSR searches, and confirmation of the share transfer chain and the Seller's authority. Title should also sit outside the general regime.

**DD-006 export/privacy incident.** The Seller characterises the matter as preliminary and immaterial, while disclosing that the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps) and that whether anyone accessed the file is unknown (DL 6). We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount. We should, however, require the Seller to preserve logs, investigate the scope and access, and provide regular updates. Consider a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident; this is a recommendation for the deal team to assess rather than a stated playbook position.

**Ironquay IP.** The AUD 180k open SOW3 amount is recorded as open but is not independently verified (DL 4). Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on payment (DD-004 clause 7.3). The indemnity should be broadened beyond the SOW3 payment and must preserve the SOW3 cure. We should obtain payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs, but the disclosure does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued (DL 8). Assess them commercially. Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from the price.

**Items outside the playbook (flag for review).** The office lease (DL 7) notification obligation and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DL 9) are not confirmed as requiring landlord or Mossvale consent to the share sale, and the disclosure does not say they do not. Ask for the lease and Mossvale provisions and a written analysis of whether any consent is required.

**Stale disclosure.** The disclosure speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure before signing and Completion.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Caps and thresholds:** Counter at a 25% / AUD 6m general cap, AUD 5k de minimis, and AUD 50k first-dollar tipping basket. Do not accept the 20% cap or 18-month period unless Amelia Frost gives written approval identifying the draft.
2. **Fundamental/Title:** Create a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the "same as general" proposal.
3. **Fraud carve-out:** Add a non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
4. **Disclosure:** Delete general disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers. Accept only specific fair disclosure.
5. **Buyer knowledge:** Delete clause 8.3.
6. **Bluefen:** Make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition.
7. **Riverlark:** Require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. **Bonuses:** Add the AUD 420k and quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded item.
9. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain payment evidence or confirmatory assignment.
10. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, investigation, and periodic updates. Consider a specific indemnity. Do not treat the matter as confirmed or immaterial.
11. **Sandbar:** Assess commercially. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
12. **Tax and IP:** Keep open and in separate categories. Do not fold into the general regime, and do not assume unlimited liability or resolution.
13. **Title:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient on its own.
14. **Lease and Mossvale:** Obtain the provisions and a written consent analysis.
15. **Bring-down:** Require an updated disclosure letter before signing and Completion.

Recommend that the responsible NSW lawyer confirm the drafting of these changes before the mark-up goes to the Seller.

question: SPA-N-016 (Tax/IP open terms). Seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment. What does the advice recommend relative to the seller's position?
text:
Of course. Here is a detailed review of the Seller's documents against the Wattlebridge Holdings negotiation playbook for Project Kestrel, with reasoning and recommendations.

### Executive Summary

The Seller's draft represents a significant departure from our playbook in nearly every material area. Their proposal systematically weakens our core protections by attempting to:
1.  **Lower financial caps and thresholds** across the board.
2.  **Subject Fundamental/Title claims to the same restrictive general regime** we reject for general claims.
3.  **Implement broad, "deemed disclosure" and buyer-knowledge exclusions** that would nullify specific indemnities and shift risk back to us.
4.  **Fail to provide concrete, pre-completion solutions** for critical issues like Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment, and employee bonuses.

Our pushback must be firm and principled, grounded in our playbook positions. The strategy should be to reject the Seller's attempt to create a "lowest common denominator" liability framework and instead re-anchor the negotiation to our baseline positions.

---

### Detailed Analysis of Departures & Recommended Pushback

#### 1. General Warranty Cap (Clause 12.1)
*   **Seller's Position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
*   **Playbook Position:** Baseline 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost, which has not been given.
*   **Departure:** The Seller has unilaterally adopted our conditional fallback without authorization.
*   **Reasoning:** This is a clear negotiation tactic to anchor the discussion at a lower number. Accepting it without resistance would set a poor precedent and forfeit a significant bargaining chip.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Re-state our baseline of 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If Amelia Frost's authority is later obtained, we can use the 20% figure as a tradeable concession in exchange for other improvements (e.g., on thresholds or time limits).

#### 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)
*   **Seller's Position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; basket of AUD 250,000, with recovery only for the excess above the basket.
*   **Playbook Position:** De minimis of AUD 5,000; aggregate basket of AUD 50,000, with seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
*   **Departure:** The Seller's thresholds are significantly higher and more buyer-unfriendly. Their basket structure ("excess only") is the worst possible outcome for us.
*   **Reasoning:** High thresholds make it difficult to recover smaller but legitimate claims. An "excess only" basket means we cannot recover the first AUD 250,000 of claims, which is a major financial risk.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject firmly.** Insist on our playbook positions: AUD 5,000 de minimis and a USD 50,000 "first-dollar" basket. This is a key protection for smaller warranty breaches.

#### 3. Time Limits & Fundamental/Title Claims (Clause 12.3 / 13)
*   **Seller's Position:** General claims limited to 18 months. Proposes that **all claims** (including fundamental/title) be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for "administrative simplicity."
*   **Playbook Position:** General claims: 24 months (18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's approval). Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
*   **Departure:** This is one of the most dangerous departures. The Seller is attempting to collapse the distinct, stronger protection for fundamental warranties (title, capacity, etc.) into the weak general warranty regime.
*   **Reasoning:** If title or capacity issues arise after 18 months, or if the claim exceeds the general cap, we would have no recourse. This undermines the very foundation of the share purchase.
*   **Recommendation:** **Strongly reject.** This is non-negotiable from our perspective. We must insist on a separate, superior regime for Fundamental and Title claims as outlined in our playbook. The 18-month general claim period is also unacceptable without Amelia's approval.

#### 4. Limitations & Reliance (Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
*   **Seller's Position:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance provisions apply to **all claims of any nature**.
*   **Playbook Position:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, and exclusive remedies.
*   **Departure:** The Seller's wording attempts to apply the contractual limitations to even the most egregious conduct, which is contrary to public policy and our playbook.
*   **Reasoning:** If the Seller fraudulently conceals a material liability, we should not be bound by a cap or time limit. This is a standard and necessary protection.
*   **Recommendation:** **Insist on the insertion of explicit carve-outs** for fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct, to the maximum extent enforceable at law.

#### 5. Disclosure & Buyer Knowledge (Schedule 7, Clause 8.3)
*   **Seller's Position:** Relies on "general disclosure of the data room and public registers." Buyer has no claim for matters it or its advisers "had knowledge," including anything discoverable from the data room.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **specific fair disclosure**. Reject whole-data-room/public-register deemed disclosure. Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is using a classic "deemed disclosure" clause, which is the antithesis of our playbook. It effectively says that by giving us access to a data room, they have disclosed everything, and we are now responsible for finding any and all issues.
*   **Reasoning:** This shifts the entire burden of due diligence onto us and excuses the Seller from specifically highlighting material risks. It makes specific indemnities (like Ironquay) meaningless if the information is "in the data room."
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject the deemed disclosure concept entirely.** Demand that the Disclosure Letter contain specific, numbered disclosures of all material matters. For the buyer-knowledge clause, we must delete it or, at a minimum, limit it to the actual knowledge of specific named individuals within Wattlebridge who were involved in the transaction, after reasonable enquiry.

#### 6. Bluefen Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3)
*   **Seller's Position:** Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is proposing a weak, "best efforts" standard and a delayed confirmation that does not provide certainty at Completion. Bluefen is ~30% of revenue; this is a critical risk.
*   **Reasoning:** "Consent-on-delivery" means we could complete the transaction without having seen the final, unconditional consent, risking a post-completion termination of a major contract.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject.** We must have the final, written Bluefen consent, with evidence that all conditions precedent in clause 11.3 have been met, **as a condition precedent to Completion**. The funds should not be released until this is in our hands.

#### 7. Riverlark Facility (Clause 2 / 7)
*   **Seller's Position:** Facility (AUD 3.2M) will be addressed by a release "to be provided following Completion."
*   **Playbook Position:** Require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia's approval.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is proposing to deal with the debt *after* we have completed and paid, which is completely unacceptable.
*   **Reasoning:** This would leave us owning a company with a AUD 3.2M debt and a mere promise of a release. The transaction must be debt-free/cash-free as per our baseline.
*   **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The SPA must require the Riverlark facility to be repaid in full from the Completion funds, with all security released, **prior to or at Completion**. The funds flow must reflect this direct repayment.

#### 8. Employee Bonuses (DD-005 / Funds Flow)
*   **Seller's Position:** Bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.
*   **Playbook Position:** Bonuses must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to avoid accountability for these accrued liabilities post-completion.
*   **Reasoning:** If these bonuses are not paid from the sale proceeds, they may become our liability as the new employer. The funds flow must be transparent.
*   **Recommendation:** **Insist on specific treatment.** The AUD 420,000 (plus any triggered on-costs) must be included as a specific line item in the Completion funds flow, to be paid to the employees or reimbursed to us by the Seller. It cannot be a silent item.

#### 9. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)
*   **Seller's Position:** Existing indemnity is "limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is considered adequate."
*   **Playbook Position:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
*   **Departure:** The Seller is refusing to broaden their indemnity for a known, unresolved IP matter.
*   **Reasoning:** The current indemnity is too narrow. If the claim is broader than just the SOW3 payment, we have no protection.
*   **Recommendation:** **Push back.** We need an indemnity that covers the entire Ironquay matter, not just one potential payment. The issue of the AUD 180,000 must be resolved, and we should seek a warranty that the amount is not owed or a specific indemnity to cover it if it is.

#### 10. Other Issues
*   **Sandbar Renewals:** The Seller's position is acceptable (ordinary-course costs). No pushback required.
*   **Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006):** The Seller's disclosure is appropriately cautious. We should preserve our rights by ensuring the SPA does not contain any warranties that we have confirmed a breach or that limit our ability to investigate further.
*   **Title (DD-012):** The Seller relying solely on the internal share register is insufficient. We must require independent title evidence (e.g., a title report, share certificates) as per our playbook.

### Summary of Recommendations

1.  **Reject the entire liability framework.** Do not engage on the specifics of their low caps and high thresholds. Re-anchor the negotiation to our **playbook baselines**.
2.  **Non-Negotiable Positions:**
    *   Separate, superior regime for **Fundamental/Title claims** (100% cap, 6+ years).
    *   **Carve-outs** for fraud/wilful concealment from all limitations.
    *   **Specific disclosure** in the Disclosure Letter, not deemed disclosure.
    *   **Pre-completion conditions** for Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment.
3.  **Key Pushback Points:**
    *   **General Warranty Cap:** Insist on 25% / AUD 6M. The 20% figure is only a fallback with Amelia's approval.
    *   **Thresholds:** Insist on AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k first-dollar basket.
    *   **General Claims Period:** Insist on 24 months.
    *   **Buyer Knowledge:** Delete the blanket exclusion or limit it to named individuals.
    *   **Employee Bonuses:** Must be a transparent line item in the funds flow.
    *   **Ironquay IP:** Demand a broader indemnity.
4.  **Negotiation Strategy:** Frame our response not as a series of counter-proposals to their low positions, but as a restatement of our standard, principled positions for a transaction of this nature. Use the Seller's draft as evidence that they are seeking to shift unacceptable risk onto us.

# Seller Compliance Review — Project Kestrel

Below is a clause-by-clause comparison against the Wattlebridge playbook, with departures flagged and recommended counters. I have grouped related issues but flagged each for senior attention because several overlap materially.

---

## 1. General warranty cap (Clause 12.1) — **conditional fallback not authorised**

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 presented as firm position.
**Playbook:** Starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20%/AUD 4,800,000 is a conditional fallback that requires *prior written* authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — and none has been given.

**Issue:** The Seller presents the reduced cap unconditionally, failing to acknowledge the conditional nature. The $1.2M reduction drops our baseline recovery by nearly half.

**Recommendation:** Do not accept the 20% cap as effective until Amelia authorises it, in writing, with the draft identified. Alternatively, hold to 25%/AUD 6,000,000 as the binding position and treat the 20%/AUD 4,800,000 only as a permitted fallback subject to a formal rider. Either way, insist on an explicit amendment exposing the condition.

---

## 2. Thresholds (Clause 12.2) — **threshold positions materially weaker**

**Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; aggregate basket AUD 250,000; excess above basket recoverable.
**Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000; once exceeded, seller liable from the first dollar (no bespoke escape).

**Issue:** Two problems. First, the de minimis of AUD 25,000 is four times our AUD 5,000 — small claims that would otherwise clear the floor become actionable early. Second, the AUD 250,000 basket means once aggregate claims exceed that, only the excess above is recovered (a substantial escape hatch for the seller). Our lower baseline means the seller bears losses on smaller dollar claims and recovers fully through lower thresholds.

**Recommendation:** Renegotiate to AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with seller liability from the first dollar once exceeded.

---

## 3. Time limits (Clause 12.3 / 13) — **unauthorised 18-month window**

**Seller:** 18 months; limitations apply to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
**Playbook:** 24 months standard; 18 months a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval — none given.

**Issue:** The Seller does not acknowledge that 18 months is itself a conditional fallback requiring Amelia’s prior written authorisation. Combined with the threshold issue above, this compacts our recovery window.

**Recommendation:** Keep 24 months as the standard notice period. Where you wish to support a shorter period, require an Amelia Frost-signed exception rider. The Seller must not foreclose this option without authorisation.

---

## 4. Fundamental / Title — **collapsed into general regime**

**Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties.
**Playbook:** Separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

**Issue:** Collapsing title into the general regime is a significant structural departure. A fundamental title defect discovered late would therefore benefit from the 20% cap rather than the 100% cap. The Seller has also failed to impose the longer statute of limitations required for title defects.

**Recommendation:** Demote title to a distinct category with a 100% cap and a ≥6-year limitation. Ensure the scheme explicitly excludes title from the general basket, de minimis, buyer-knowledge bar and the 18-month window where applicable.

---

## 5. Limitations, exclusivity & non-reliance (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) — **carve-out omitted**

**Seller:** Applies to all claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. No one may waive this.

**Issue:** The Seller’s “all claims” language is an implicit waiver of the carve-out the playbook demands. Any breach relying on fraud or concealment would then fall within a capped, limited, time-limited and non-reliance framework, which is precisely the risk we are seeking to escape.

**Recommendation:** Add a carve-out identical in substance to the playbook’s: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. Insert an explicit no-waiver provision.

---

## 6. Buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3) — **blanket exclusion overbroad**

**Seller:** No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
**Playbook:** Delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Issue:** The Seller’s inclusion of “any matter discoverable from the data room or public records” collapses the distinction between buyer knowledge and seller-knowledge-diligence that the playbook protects. This would allow the seller to exclude virtually every diligence discovery as buyer-acquired knowledge.

**Recommendation:** Delete the clause entirely. Any qualifier must name specific seller knowledge persons and specify the reasonable enquiries made. Titles, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities cannot be excused under any variant.

---

## 7. Bluefen change-control consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3) — **adequacy of consent unproven**

**Seller:** Consent addressed; uses reasonable endeavours; treats consent as satisfied on delivery.
**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence that associated conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for a material customer consent.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "market context" framing

The Seller's covering note says the [STANDARD] clauses were "reviewed and cleared by both sides," that the positions were "settled at principal level," and that only [OPEN] items need review. These are the counterparty's own assertions. Nothing in our record confirms them, and no clause is actually marked [OPEN]. Accepting the framing would mean not reviewing the package at all. I have therefore reviewed every item on its merits.

The "market context" ranges are also unsupported advocacy. Even on the Seller's own figures, it has taken the most seller-friendly end of every range. **Action:** before the mark-up goes out, confirm with Wattlebridge's principals whether anything was in fact agreed at principal level. If so, check exactly what and at what level of detail.

The Disclosure Letter is notably more candid than the cover note. It confirms that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and incident investigation are all **unresolved**, and that the bonuses are **not in the funds flow**. The cover note's descriptions ("addressed," "adequate," "not material," "ordinary course") are not supported by the Seller's own disclosures.

---

## 1. Price and funds flow (highest priority)

The deal is debt-free/cash-free at AUD 24m. Several Company liabilities are being left inside the business while the Seller takes the full price.

| Item | Amount | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (DD-003) | ~AUD 3.2m | Release "following Completion" | Repay at Completion out of the price |
| Completion bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k plus on-costs | "Matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Deduct as a Transaction Expense or Indebtedness |
| Ironquay SOW3 fees (DD-010) | AUD 180k open (unverified) | Not addressed | Treat as debt-like if payable; pay at Completion |
| Sandbar renewals (DD-008/011) | AUD 330k | "Ordinary course" | Investigate; possible debt-like or leakage item |

That is **about AUD 3.8m of identified debt and debt-like items before on-costs**, roughly 16% of the price.

**Riverlark.** A post-Completion release is unacceptable on a debt-free deal.
- The change-control clause (8.1) may put the facility into default the moment the shares transfer.
- Security would stay over the Company's assets in the meantime.
- Require a payoff letter, a deed of release, PPSR discharge (and ASIC charge documents if relevant) delivered **at Completion**, with the payoff paid directly to Riverlark from the price.
- Confirm there is no share mortgage over the Paperbark shares, as that would also go to title.

**Bonuses.** The Company is the employer, so the liability, and any PAYG withholding, superannuation, payroll tax and workers' comp on-costs, sits with the Company and therefore with us.
- Calling them "a matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the price is reduced.
- Require the gross amount plus all on-costs to be deducted from the price, or funded by the Seller and paid through payroll at Completion.
- Back this with a specific indemnity. Confirm the continued-employment conditions do not leave a tail liability after Completion.

---

## 2. Liability regime (cl. 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

**Cap (12.1), 20% / AUD 4.8m.** This is the top of the Seller's own range and is only modestly above the identified debt items alone. Push for a higher general cap; it can be traded against W&I cover if one is being used. More importantly, the cap must apply **only to general warranty claims**. It should not apply to title/capacity, tax, specific indemnities, leakage/price adjustment, covenant breaches, or fraud.

**Thresholds (12.2).**
- The AUD 250k basket (~1.04%) is structured as a **deductible** ("only the excess"). Seek a **tipping basket**, so that once the threshold is crossed the whole amount is recoverable, and ideally a lower threshold.
- On the AUD 25k de minimis: claims arising from the same or related facts should aggregate.
- Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax or indemnity claims.

**Time limits (12.3/13).** 18 months is acceptable for general warranties, at most. Reject the proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." It reverses the proper default and could quietly catch indemnities and tax. Instead:
- Tax: the relevant statutory amendment/assessment period plus a buffer (commonly 5–7 years).
- Title/capacity: 6–7 years or the statutory limitation period.
- Specific indemnities: their own tailored periods.

**Fundamental warranties.** Reject applying the general caps and time limits to title and capacity "for administrative simplicity." If the Seller does not own or cannot sell the shares, we have bought nothing. These warranties should be:
- capped at 100% of the price;
- free of any basket or de minimis;
- subject to a long survival period.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying "to all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5).** Require express carve-outs for:
- fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its agents;
- specific indemnities;
- tax;
- leakage and price adjustment;
- the Seller's covenants.

Under NSW law, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses also interact with misleading or deceptive conduct claims under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. They may not fully exclude that liability, but we should not concede drafting that attempts to. NSW counsel should confirm the final wording.

---

## 3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (DL 1.1–1.2).** This would effectively hollow out the warranties: any document anywhere in the data room qualifies every warranty. Push for:
- only **specific disclosures**, fairly made with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter;
- data room documents to count only where specifically referenced against the relevant warranty;
- public registers limited to searches actually conducted and identified, if accepted at all;
- **no general disclosure** against fundamental warranties, tax or specific indemnities.

**Stale disclosure date.** The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, more than six weeks before today. Require an updated data room index and bring-down information. Any supplementary disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion should not cure a breach without Buyer consent, and should give a walk-away right if material.

**Disclosure Letter cl. 1.4 ("no admission").** This is tolerable as a statement that the Seller admits nothing. It should not be read as diluting the factual content of the specific disclosures in cl. 2–10, which we will rely on.

**Buyer knowledge (8.3).** Reject this. It bars claims for anything the Buyer *or its advisers* knew **or could have discovered** from the data room or public records. That is constructive knowledge and it guts the warranty package. Preferred position: an express statement that Buyer knowledge does not limit claims. Fallback: limit it to the *actual* knowledge of named Wattlebridge deal-team individuals, of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.

---

## 4. Specific matters

**Bluefen (DD-002). Critical, about 30% of revenue.**
- "Reasonable endeavours" plus treating the condition as satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent is inadequate.
- The consent must be a **condition precedent** that is unconditional, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably. It must evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied and must not vary pricing or terms adversely.
- The CP should be waivable **only by the Buyer**, with a long-stop date and a walk right.
- Ideally, require best endeavours from the Seller and a pre-Completion covenant to keep the Buyer informed and involved in communications with Bluefen.
- If Bluefen terminates or adversely varies within an agreed period after Completion, consider a price adjustment or escrow.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004/DD-010).** The existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is not adequate. Under clause 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials occurs only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it uses, not merely an unpaid AUD 180k. Require:
- verification of the payment position, with the fee paid from the price at Completion if outstanding;
- a **confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP**;
- a specific indemnity covering loss from any failure to own the SOW3 materials, infringement claims, and the cost of re-development or licensing. It should sit outside the cap and thresholds and carry a longer survival period.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006).** Do not accept "preliminary, not expected to be material." About 1,240 personal-information records were sent to an unintended external recipient. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Part IIIC), an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days of becoming aware of it. That window may already have closed, so a missed assessment or notification is itself a risk. Require:
- the incident timeline, the investigation findings to date, and any forensic report;
- a pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and make any required notifications, with Buyer consultation;
- a specific indemnity outside the cap and thresholds covering regulatory, remediation, notification and third-party claims;
- tightened privacy and data-security warranties, specifically disclosed against only this incident;
- consideration of an escrow or retention.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011), 3 × AUD 110k.** Three related renewals at identical amounts that the Seller itself says should be "read together" raise a question of whether they were split to stay below an approval or conduct-of-business threshold. "Related" also needs clarifying: is Sandbar a Seller-related party? Require:
- copies of the renewals, their timing against the signing and locked-box dates, and their terms on termination and committed spend;
- confirmation of whether any were entered into after the conduct-of-business covenants applied;
- if they are Seller-related or outside ordinary course, treatment as leakage or a price deduction, or termination before Completion at the Seller's cost.

**Tax and IP "settled under the general regime."** Not agreed. We need:
- a standalone **tax indemnity/covenant** for pre-Completion tax, outside the cap and thresholds, with a statutory-period survival;
- IP warranties with a cap and survival appropriate to a SaaS business, where IP is core value. Consider treating them as quasi-fundamental.

**Title (DD-012).** The share register alone is not enough. Require:
- a fundamental title warranty that the shares are free of encumbrances, options and rights of pre-emption;
- reconciliation against ASIC records;
- delivery of share certificates, or lost-certificate indemnities;
- confirmation of no Riverlark or other security over the shares;
- any constitutional or shareholder-agreement pre-emption waivers.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller's characterisation (notification only; no change-of-control trigger) is plausible but untested. Have our team review both provisions directly. Ensure the lease notification is given in time, as a Seller covenant. For Mossvale, check for any deemed-assignment or change-of-control wording. If it is ambiguous, obtain a comfort letter.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Must-haves (deal-critical):**
1. Reject the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing. Confirm internally what, if anything, principals agreed.
2. Funds flow: deduct Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) and the bonuses (AUD 420k plus all on-costs) at Completion. Treat the Ironquay fee as debt-like if payable. Riverlark payoff letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion.
3. Bluefen consent as a Buyer-waivable CP, unconditional or on acceptable terms, with the clause 11.3 conditions evidenced and a walk right.
4. Fundamental (title/capacity) warranties capped at 100% of price, no thresholds, long survival.
5. Fraud carve-out from all limitations, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions.
6. Delete constructive buyer knowledge (8.3). Replace with no-knowledge-limitation or actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters.
7. Specific disclosure only. No general data room or public-register disclosure, and none at all against fundamentals, tax or indemnities.

**Strongly recommended:**

8. Specific indemnities, outside the cap and thresholds, for: the DD-006 incident, Ironquay IP ownership, the bonuses and on-costs, and pre-Completion tax.
9. Ironquay confirmatory assignment as a CP.
10. Tipping basket; aggregation of related claims for de minimis.
11. Reverse the "limitations apply to all Claims" default. Set tailored survival periods for tax, title and indemnities.
12. Updated disclosure and data room bring-down; no cure of breaches by supplementary disclosure.
13. Escrow or retention sized to the Bluefen, incident and Ironquay exposures, or W&I insurance with Seller-funded specific indemnities for known risks, which W&I typically excludes.

**Negotiable, depending on overall package:**

14. Level of the general cap (20% is the ceiling of the Seller's range, not a floor for us).
15. Basket quantum.
16. Sandbar: depending on what diligence shows, treat as leakage or a price adjustment, or accept with a specific warranty.
17. Lease and Mossvale: accept the Seller's characterisation subject to our own review and a covenant to give notices.

**Information requests to send now:** the Bluefen consent status and correspondence; the Riverlark payoff figure; the bonus terms and on-cost calculation; Ironquay payment evidence; the DD-006 timeline and investigation report; the Sandbar contracts and approval history; ASIC extracts and share certificates; and an updated data room index.

*Please treat this as a working analysis for the deal team. Final positions on the ACL interaction, the NDB timing and the tax survival periods should be confirmed by NSW and tax counsel.*

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline points

1. **Do not accept the "[STANDARD]" labels or the "Reviewer Efficiency Note."** These are the Seller's own unilateral tags. Nothing in the package shows that the Buyer agreed to any of them. Almost every material issue below sits under a "[STANDARD]" label. The note also asserts that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We should reject that in writing so it cannot later be used as evidence of agreement. I have reviewed every position on its merits.
2. **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note.** Bluefen is described as "addressed," but the letter says no consent has been obtained. The DD-006 incident is called "not expected to be material," but the letter says the investigation is preliminary and its scope is unknown. The bonuses are called "a matter for the Seller," but they are Company liabilities and are missing from the funds flow.
3. **The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026, about six weeks old.** We need an updated letter and a bring-down before signing.

---

## A. Limitation package

### 1. General cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m), cl 12.1
- 20% for general warranties is within the market range. We can accept it or open at 30–35% as a trade.
- The real issue is scope. The cap must not apply to:
  - fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority);
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
  - the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark);
  - leakage or price-adjustment claims;
  - breach of covenants;
  - fraud or wilful concealment.

### 2. Thresholds, cl 12.2
- **Basket of AUD 250k (about 1.04% of price), deductible only:** this is high and purely Seller-friendly. Push for about AUD 120k (0.5%) as a tipping basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed.
- **De minimis of AUD 25k:** reduce to AUD 10–15k. Related or same-cause claims should aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- Thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.

### 3. Time limits, cl 12.3/13
- 18 months for general warranties is acceptable. It covers at least one full audit cycle.
- **Reject the default that "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."** Reverse it so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Proposed periods:
  - Title and capacity: at least 7 years, or the statutory limitation period.
  - Tax: the ATO amendment period plus 6 months. This is unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - Specific indemnities: matched to the risk. For example, DD-006 should run at least 3 years, given regulatory and class-action exposure.

### 4. Fundamental/title warranties under the same cap and time limits
- **Reject.** Title is the entire subject matter of the deal. If title fails, we have bought nothing, so recovery must be capped at 100% of the price (AUD 24m) with the long survival period above.
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept this.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature," cl 9.3/12.8/20.5
- **Carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment** by the Seller, its officers or its advisers. Under NSW law the Seller cannot exclude liability for its own fraud. An attempt to do so invites a dispute, so express carve-outs are needed.
- Exclusive remedy should not cover specific performance, injunctions, leakage or price adjustment, or covenant breaches.
- Non-reliance clauses do not reliably exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s18. We should not be giving up that protection for pre-contract statements made outside the warranties. This includes the cover-note characterisations such as "Bluefen addressed" and "not material." If the Seller stands by those statements, they should become warranties.

---

## B. Disclosure framework

### 6. General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
- **Reject.** This puts the cost of the Seller's information onto the Buyer and makes the warranties largely illusory. Our position:
  - Only specific disclosures that are fair and give sufficient detail for a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter count.
  - Data room documents count only where specifically referenced in the Disclosure Letter.
  - No general disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records." At most, accept limited specified searches as at a fixed date, such as ASIC and PPSR.
  - Disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, tax warranties or any indemnity.
  - The data room is to be frozen and supplied on USB/archive as an agreed index.
- **Clause 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in principle. However, we should ensure it does not weaken the effect of the specific disclosures as facts.

### 7. Buyer knowledge, cl 8.3
- **Reject in current form.** It reaches constructive knowledge ("discoverable") and advisers' knowledge, which would effectively wipe out the warranties.
- **Primary position:** express pro-sandbagging. Buyer knowledge does not limit claims.
- **Fallback:** actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals only, limited to facts fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and never applicable to indemnities.

---

## C. Specific issues

### 8. Bluefen consent (about AUD 3.6m revenue, about 30%), cl 3/6.3
- The letter confirms no final consent exists and that the cl 11.3 conditions have not been shown to be satisfied. "Addressed" is wrong.
- The Seller's mechanism treats the condition as satisfied on mere delivery of a written consent, even if the consent is conditional, partial, or comes with changed terms. Our position:
  - A **Condition Precedent** to Completion: unconditional written consent in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, acting reasonably.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived.
  - No adverse amendments to the contract, such as pricing, term or termination rights.
  - The CP can be waived **only by the Buyer**.
  - The Seller uses **best (or all reasonable) endeavours**, not reasonable endeavours.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.
  - A warranty at Completion that Bluefen has not given notice of termination or non-renewal.

### 9. Riverlark facility (about AUD 3.2m), cl 2/7
- **A release "following Completion" is unacceptable** on a debt-free/cash-free deal. A change of control under cl 8.1 may itself trigger default or acceleration.
- Required at Completion:
  - A payoff letter confirming the exact payout figure and per-diem amount.
  - Repayment directly from the purchase price via the funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - A deed of release.
  - PPSR discharges and the release of any guarantees or share security, which we need to check: Riverlark may hold security over the shares, which also goes to title.
  - All delivered as Completion deliverables.

### 10. DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k)
- These are Company obligations, not "a matter for the Seller."
- Treat them as **Transaction Expenses/Debt deducted from the price**, grossed up for:
  - employer superannuation (check whether the bonuses count as OTE);
  - payroll tax;
  - workers' compensation and other on-costs.
- They should be paid through the Company's payroll at or immediately after Completion, with PAYG withheld and funded by the Seller.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall or later claims, including claims from employees who do not meet the continued-employment condition.
- The funds flow must itemise all of this.

### 11. Ironquay / SOW3 IP, cl 11.1
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 materials does **not pass** until every SOW3 fee has cleared. AUD 180k is shown as open. So the Company may not currently own IP it relies on.
- An indemnity limited to "the SOW3 payment" does not cover the real risk: loss of the IP, infringement claims, or re-development costs. Our position:
  - Payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion, with a bank-verified receipt. This should be a CP or Completion deliverable, or at minimum the AUD 180k is retained or deducted.
  - A **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay as a Completion deliverable.
  - A broadened indemnity for all Losses arising from the Company not owning, or not being free to use, the SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with at least 3–6 years survival.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident, cl 4.6/Sched 6
- About 1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are unresolved.
- Under the Privacy Act NDB scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days. The incident predates 22 September, so we need to know whether that assessment has been completed and whether the OAIC or affected individuals have been notified. A failure here is an exposure in its own right.
- "Not expected to be material" has no stated basis. Our position:
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment, follow forensic or legal advice, and notify if required, with Buyer consultation.
  - Delivery of the investigation report.
  - A **specific indemnity** covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, and third-party or class claims. It should sit outside the cap and basket, not be qualified by disclosure, and survive at least 3 years.
  - Consider an escrow or retention of about AUD 0.5–1m pending resolution.
  - The privacy and data warranties must not be read down by this disclosure.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (3 × AUD 110k = AUD 330k)
- Three linked renewals of identical value suggest a commitment split to stay below an approval threshold. The Seller's own letter says they should be read together.
- Points to raise:
  - Ask for dates, terms and termination rights, and for confirmation of whether the renewals were entered into or committed after the accounts date.
  - Any renewal after signing must require Buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenants, with the relevant thresholds aggregated for related contracts.
  - Where the renewals are prepaid or accrued and not ordinary course, treat them as leakage or as a completion accounts adjustment.
  - Verify there is no related-party element.

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
- **Reject.** We need a standalone **tax indemnity/deed** for pre-Completion tax:
  - capped at 100% of the price;
  - no basket;
  - not qualified by disclosure;
  - survival aligned to the amendment period.
- IP warranties covering ownership and non-infringement are core value for an analytics business. Push for a higher sub-cap of 50–100% and longer survival. Ironquay shows these risks are real.

### 15. Title evidenced only by the share register (DD-012)
- The share register is the Seller's own record. The letter itself notes that the Buyer has not verified it. We require:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - the issue and transfer history;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other share rights exist;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares;
  - a release of any security over the shares, including from Riverlark;
  - signed share transfer forms at Completion.
- The title warranty is fundamental (see point 4).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- The Seller's characterisations ("notification only"; "no consent merely because shares are sold") need to be checked by our own team against the full change-of-control and "assignment" definitions. Some leases and contracts treat a change in control as a deemed assignment.
- Add any required notices as Completion deliverables or post-Completion covenants.
- Include a warranty that no consent is required beyond those listed.

### 17. Staleness and bring-down
- The letter is dated 22 September 2026.
- Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing.
- Warranties should be repeated at Completion. Any new disclosures at Completion should **not** cure breaches; at most, they give the Buyer a termination right.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "[STANDARD]" labels / efficiency note | Pre-cleared; review only [OPEN] | Reject in writing; no positions agreed |
| 1 | General cap | 20% (AUD 4.8m), applies broadly | Accept 20–35% for **general warranties only** |
| 2 | Basket / de minimis | AUD 250k deductible / AUD 25k | About AUD 120k tipping / AUD 10–15k; aggregation |
| 3 | Time limits | 18m, default applies to all claims | 18m general only; title 7y+; tax = amendment period + 6m; indemnities 3y+ |
| 4 | Fundamental warranties | Same cap and time limits | 100% cap; long survival; not disclosable against |
| 5 | Limitations / non-reliance | All Claims of any nature | Carve out fraud/concealment, indemnities, tax, covenants, leakage |
| 6 | Disclosure | General disclosure of data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; none against fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Actual + constructive + advisers | Pro-sandbagging; fallback actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 8 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | Buyer-waivable CP; unconditional consent; 11.3 satisfied; best endeavours |
| 9 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release post-Completion | Payoff from price at Completion; deed of release; PPSR discharges |
| 10 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | Deduct as Transaction Expenses incl. on-costs; payroll mechanics; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Pay before Completion; confirmatory assignment; full IP-loss indemnity |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | NDB compliance covenant; report; uncapped specific indemnity; retention |
| 13 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Full details; aggregate consent thresholds; leakage/adjustment treatment |
| 14 | Tax / IP | General regime | Standalone tax indemnity; enhanced IP sub-cap and survival |
| 15 | Title | Share register only | Independent verification; release of share security; transfers at Completion |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify ourselves; notices as deliverables; consents warranty |
| 17 | Stale disclosure | Dated 22 Sept 2026 | Updated letter; bring-down; no cure by later disclosure |

**Priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Disclosure and knowledge framework (6, 7).
2. Fundamental, tax and fraud carve-outs (4, 5, 14).
3. Price-protection items: Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay AUD 180k (9, 10, 11). Together these are about AUD 3.8m or more of value that must come off the price or be resolved at Completion.
4. Bluefen CP (8).
5. DD-006 indemnity and retention (12).
6. Threshold and cap tuning (1–3), which can be used as trading currency.

Our own diligence findings should be checked against the Seller's characterisations of the lease, Mossvale and Sandbar before we finalise these positions.
